title.raw: 卷108之三 禮志四之三 Volume 108c Treatise 4: Rituals 3

sentences.zh: 魏自太祖至於武泰帝，及太皇太后、皇太后、皇后崩，悉依漢魏既葬公除。

translations.literal: From Taizu through the Wutai Emperor, whenever a Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, or Empress died, Wei uniformly followed the Han and Wei practice of public removal of mourning after burial.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu down to the Wutai Emperor, whenever a grand empress dowager, empress dowager, or empress died, the Wei court uniformly followed the Han and Wei custom of ending public mourning once the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 唯高祖太和十四年文明太后崩，將營山陵，九月，安定王休，齊郡王簡，咸陽王禧，河南王幹，廣陵王羽，潁川王雍，始平王勰，北海王詳，侍中、太尉、錄尚書事、東陽王丕，侍中、司徒、淮陽王尉元，侍中、司空、長樂王穆亮，侍中、尚書左僕射、平原王陸叡等，率百僚詣闕表曰：「上靈不弔，大行太皇太后崩背，溥天率土，痛慕斷絕。

translations.literal: Only when Empress Dowager Wenming died in the fourteenth year of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, as the imperial tomb was to be prepared—in the ninth month, Prince of Anding Xiu, Prince of Qijun Jian, Prince of Xianyang Xi, Prince of Henan Gan, Prince of Guangling Yu, Prince of Yingchuan Yong, Prince of Shiping Rui, Prince of Beihai Xiang, Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Dongyang Wang Pi, Palace Attendant and Minister of Education and Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, Palace Attendant and Minister of Works and Prince of Changle Mu Liang, Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Pingyuan Lu Rui, and others led the hundred officials to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: 'Heaven does not comfort us; the Grand Empress Dowager has passed away; all under heaven and across the land, grief and longing are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Empress Dowager Wenming died in the fourteenth year of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, as work on her imperial tomb was about to begin—in the ninth month, the Prince of Anding, Xiu; the Prince of Qijun, Jian; the Prince of Xianyang, Xi; the Prince of Henan, Gan; the Prince of Guangling, Yu; the Prince of Yingchuan, Yong; the Prince of Shiping, Rui; the Prince of Beihai, Xiang; Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Dongyang, Pi; Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Prince of Huaiyang, Wei Yuan; Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Prince of Changle, Mu Liang; Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Pingyuan, Lu Rui; and others led the full bureaucracy to the palace gate and submitted a memorial: 'Heaven offers no comfort; the Grand Empress Dowager has departed; all under heaven and across the land, grief and longing are cut off.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下孝思烝烝，攀號罔極。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty's filial thoughts are abundant and unceasing, your cries of grief without limit.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that Your Majesty's filial devotion is deep and unceasing, your cries of grief beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 臣等聞先王制禮，必有隨世之變；

translations.literal: We your subjects have heard that when the former kings established ritual, there were necessarily changes with the age;
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that when the former kings established ritual, they necessarily adapted it to the times;

sentences.zh: 前賢創法，亦務適時之宜。

translations.literal: when former worthies created law, they also strove for what suited the time.
translations.idiomatic: and when former worthies created institutions, they too sought what suited the age.

sentences.zh: 良以世代不同，古今異致故也。

translations.literal: Truly because generations differ and ancient and modern circumstances differ.
translations.idiomatic: This is simply because generations differ and ancient and modern circumstances are not the same.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，雖則自古，然中代已後，未之能行。

translations.literal: Three-year mourning, though ancient, since the middle ages has not been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Three-year mourning, though ancient in origin, has not been practiced since the middle dynasties.

sentences.zh: 先朝成式，事在可準，聖后終制，刊之金冊。

translations.literal: The former court's established form is a matter that may be taken as standard; the Holy Empress's final regulations were inscribed in the golden book.
translations.idiomatic: The former court's established precedent may be followed; the Holy Empress's final regulations were recorded in the golden book.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下至孝發衷，哀毀過禮，欲依上古，喪終三年。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty's utmost filial piety arises from the heart, your grief and emaciation exceed ritual propriety, and you wish to follow high antiquity and mourn to the end of three years.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that Your Majesty's utmost filial piety wells from the heart, that your grief and emaciation exceed ritual propriety, and that you wish to follow high antiquity and observe mourning for the full three years.

sentences.zh: 誠協大舜孝慕之德，實非俯遵濟世之道。

translations.literal: It truly accords with the virtue of Shun's filial longing, but in fact does not bow to follow the way of succoring the age.
translations.idiomatic: This truly accords with the virtue of Shun's filial longing, but it does not bow to the way of governing and succoring the realm.

sentences.zh: 今雖中夏穆清，庶邦康靜，然萬機事殷，不可暫曠，春秋烝嘗，事難廢闕。

translations.literal: Now although the central lands are tranquil and clear and the myriad states are peaceful and still, yet the myriad affairs of state are pressing and may not be briefly neglected; the spring and autumn offerings are matters hard to omit.
translations.idiomatic: Although the central lands are now tranquil and the myriad states at peace, the myriad affairs of state are pressing and cannot be set aside even briefly; the spring and autumn sacrifices are duties that cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，抑至孝之深誠，副億兆之企望，喪期禮數，一從終制，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: We humbly wish Heaven's discernment to restrain the deepest sincerity of utmost filial piety, answer the hopes of the hundred millions, and let mourning period and ritual numbers uniformly follow the final regulations—then all under heaven would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Heaven may restrain the deepest sincerity of your utmost filial piety, answer the hopes of the hundred millions, and let the mourning period and ritual observances follow the final regulations uniformly—then all under heaven would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 日月有期，山陵將就，請展安兆域，以備奉終之禮。」

translations.literal: The sun and moon have their term; the mountain tomb will soon be completed—we request to extend and settle the auspicious burial ground to prepare the rites of final service.'
translations.idiomatic: The appointed day draws near and the imperial tomb will soon be completed—we ask that the auspicious burial ground be prepared so that the rites of final service may be performed.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凶禍甫爾，未忍所請。」

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Disaster has only just occurred; I cannot bear what you request.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'Disaster has only just struck; I cannot bear to grant what you request.'

sentences.zh: 休等又表曰：「臣等聞五帝已前，喪期無數，三代相因，禮制始立，名雖虛置，行之者寡。

translations.literal: Xiu and others again submitted a memorial: 'We your subjects have heard that before the Five Emperors mourning periods had no fixed number; the Three Dynasties inherited one another and ritual institutions were first established—though the name was nominally set, few practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and the others submitted another memorial: 'We have heard that before the Five Emperors mourning periods had no fixed number; only when the Three Dynasties succeeded one another were ritual institutions first established—though the name was set in theory, few actually practiced it.

sentences.zh: 高宗徒有諒闇之言，而無可遵之式；

translations.literal: Gaozong had only words of seclusion in mourning, but no pattern that could be followed;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong spoke only of seclusion in mourning, but left no pattern that could be followed;

sentences.zh: 康王既廢初喪之儀，先行即位之禮。

translations.literal: King Kang had already abolished the rites of initial mourning and first carried out the rites of accession.
translations.idiomatic: King Kang had already set aside the rites of initial mourning and performed the accession rites first.

sentences.zh: 於是無改之道或虧，三年之喪有缺。

translations.literal: Thus the way of making no changes was sometimes impaired, and three-year mourning had gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the principle of making no changes was sometimes compromised, and three-year mourning was left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 夫豈無至孝之君，賢明之子？

translations.literal: How could there be no rulers of utmost filial piety or worthy and enlightened sons?
translations.idiomatic: Were there not rulers of utmost filial piety and worthy, enlightened sons?

sentences.zh: 皆以理貴隨時，義存百姓。

translations.literal: All took principle as valuing adaptation to the time and righteousness as residing in the welfare of the people.
translations.idiomatic: They all held that principle lay in adapting to the times and that righteousness lay in caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 是以君薨而即位，不暇改年；

translations.literal: Therefore when the ruler died they took the throne and had no leisure to change the year;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the ruler died they took the throne without waiting to change the year;

sentences.zh: 踰月而即葬，豈待同軌；

translations.literal: buried after a month—how could they wait until all roads were in mourning;
translations.idiomatic: buried after a month rather than waiting until all roads were in mourning;

sentences.zh: 葬而即吉，不必終喪。

translations.literal: after burial they at once returned to auspicious observance and need not complete the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: and after burial they at once returned to normal observance without completing the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 此乃二漢所以經綸治道，魏晉所以綱理政術。

translations.literal: This is how the two Han dynasties wove together the way of governance and how Wei and Jin structured the art of government.
translations.idiomatic: This is how the two Han dynasties organized the way of governance and how Wei and Jin structured the art of government.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以至孝之性，遭罔極之艱，永慕崩號，哀過虞舜，誠是萬古之高德，曠世之絕軌。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, with a nature of utmost filial piety, has encountered boundless hardship, forever longing and crying in grief, sorrow surpassing Yu Shun—truly virtue of ten thousand ages and a track unmatched through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that Your Majesty, with a nature of utmost filial piety, has encountered boundless hardship, forever longing and crying in grief, your sorrow surpassing even that of Shun—truly a virtue for ten thousand ages and a path unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 然天下至廣，萬機至殷，曠之一朝，庶政必滯。

translations.literal: Yet all under heaven is vast and the myriad affairs pressing; leave them idle for one morning and the hundred affairs will surely stagnate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm is vast and the myriad affairs pressing; leave them idle for a single morning and government will surely stall.

sentences.zh: 又聖后終制，已有成典，宗社廢禮，其事尤大。

translations.literal: Moreover the Holy Empress's final regulations already form an established canon; to abandon ritual for state and altars is a matter especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Holy Empress's final regulations already form an established canon; to abandon state ritual for the altars of land and grain is a matter of the greatest weight.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，抑哀毀之至誠，思在予之深責，仰遵先志典冊之文，俯哀百辟元元之請。」

translations.literal: We humbly wish Heaven's discernment to restrain the utmost sincerity of grief and emaciation, reflect on the deep charge that rests upon you, look up and follow the writings of the former will in the canonical books, look down and pity the requests of the hundred ministers and the common people.'
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Heaven may restrain the utmost sincerity of your grief and emaciation, reflect on the heavy charge that rests upon you, look up and follow the writings of your predecessors in the canonical books, and look down with pity on the pleas of the ministers and the common people.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自遭禍罰，慌惚如昨，奉侍梓宮，猶悕髣髴。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Since I encountered this disaster and punishment, I have been dazed as though it were yesterday; attending the spirit coffin, it still seems dimly present.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'Since this disaster struck, I have been dazed as though it were yesterday; attending the spirit coffin, she still seems dimly present.

sentences.zh: 山陵遷厝，所未忍聞。」

translations.literal: The removal and placement of the mountain tomb is what I cannot yet bear to hear.'
translations.idiomatic: The removal and placement of the imperial tomb is what I cannot yet bear to hear.'

sentences.zh: 十月，休等又表曰：「臣等頻煩上聞，仰申誠款，聖慕惟遠，未垂昭亮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xiu and others again submitted a memorial: 'We your subjects have repeatedly troubled Your Majesty with reports, looking up to express our sincere sentiments, but the sage's longing remains distant and clear illumination has not been granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xiu and the others submitted another memorial: 'We have repeatedly troubled Your Majesty with our reports and looked up to express our sincere sentiments, yet your sage longing remains distant and you have not granted clear illumination.

sentences.zh: 伏讀哀灼，憂心如焚。

translations.literal: We humbly read your grief, scorching as fire; our hearts burn with worry.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your grief, scorching as fire, our hearts burn with worry.

sentences.zh: 臣等聞承乾統極者宜以濟世為務，經綸天下者特以百姓為心。

translations.literal: We your subjects have heard that one who inherits Heaven and holds the ultimate position should take succoring the age as his task, and one who weaves together all under heaven should take the people as his heart.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that one who inherits Heaven and holds the supreme position should take succoring the age as his task, and one who governs all under heaven should take the welfare of the people as his heart.

sentences.zh: 故萬機在躬，周康弗獲申其慕；

translations.literal: Therefore when the myriad affairs rest on one's person, even King Kang of Zhou could not express his longing;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the myriad affairs rest on one's person, even King Kang of Zhou could not fully express his longing;

sentences.zh: 漢文作戒，孝景不得終其禮。

translations.literal: when Emperor Wen of Han made his admonition, Emperor Xiaojing could not complete his rites.
translations.idiomatic: and when Emperor Wen of Han laid down his admonition, Emperor Jing could not complete the full mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 此乃先代之成軌，近世所不易。

translations.literal: This is the established track of former ages and what recent times do not lightly change.
translations.idiomatic: This is the established precedent of former ages and what recent times do not lightly alter.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太皇太后叡聖淵識，慮及始終，明誥垂於典策，遺訓備于末命。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that the Grand Empress Dowager, wise and sage with profound understanding, thought through from beginning to end; her clear instructions were handed down in canonical records and her final teachings were complete in her last commands.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that the Grand Empress Dowager, wise and sage with profound understanding, thought through every stage from beginning to end; her clear instructions were recorded in the canonical books and her final teachings were complete in her last commands.

sentences.zh: 聿修厥德，聖人所重；

translations.literal: To continue and cultivate her virtue is what the sage valued;
translations.idiomatic: To continue and cultivate her virtue is what the sages valued;

sentences.zh: 遵承先式，臣子攸尚。

translations.literal: to follow and inherit the former pattern is what ministers and sons hold in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: and to follow and inherit the former pattern is what ministers and sons hold in highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲終上達之禮，其如黎元何？

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty wishes to complete the rites of utmost expression, what of the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Although Your Majesty wishes to complete the rites of utmost filial expression, what of the common people?

sentences.zh: 臣等不勝憂懼之誠，敢冒重陳，乞垂聽訪，以副億兆之望。」

translations.literal: We your subjects cannot overcome our sincerity of worry and fear and dare again to press our case, begging that you lend your ear and inquiry to answer the hopes of the hundred millions.'
translations.idiomatic: We cannot overcome our worry and fear and dare press our case again, begging that you lend your ear to answer the hopes of the hundred millions.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「仰尋遺旨，俯聞所奏，倍增號絕。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Looking up I trace her final will; looking down I hear what you submit—my cries of grief are doubled beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'Looking up I trace her final will; looking down I hear what you submit—my cries of grief are doubled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 山陵可依典冊，如公卿所議。

translations.literal: The mountain tomb may follow the canonical books, as the dukes and ministers discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb may follow the canonical books, as the dukes and ministers discussed.

sentences.zh: 衰服之宜，情所未忍，別當備敍在心。」

translations.literal: What is proper for mourning garments is what my feelings cannot yet bear; I will separately prepare a full statement of what is in my heart.'
translations.idiomatic: What is proper for mourning garments is what my feelings cannot yet bear; I will separately set forth what is in my heart.'

sentences.zh: 既葬，休又表曰：「奉被癸酉詔書，述遺誡之旨，昭違從之義，遵儉葬之重式，稱孝思之深誠。

translations.literal: After the burial Xiu again submitted a memorial: 'We have received the guiyou-day edict, setting forth the intent of her final admonition, making clear the meaning of departing from compliance, following the weighty form of frugal burial, and praising the deep sincerity of filial thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial Xiu submitted another memorial: 'We have received the edict of the guiyou day, setting forth the intent of her final admonition, making clear the meaning of departing from compliance, following the weighty form of frugal burial, and praising the deep sincerity of your filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 伏讀未周，悲感交切。

translations.literal: We humbly read it without finishing and grief and feeling intersect in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: We read it without finishing, grief and feeling intersecting in anguish.

sentences.zh: 日月有期，山陵即就，伏惟陛下永慕崩號，倍增摧絕。

translations.literal: The sun and moon have their term; the mountain tomb is about to be completed—we humbly consider that Your Majesty forever longs and cries in grief, your devastation doubled beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The appointed day draws near and the imperial tomb is about to be completed—we humbly note that Your Majesty forever longs and cries in grief, your devastation doubled beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 臣等具位在官，與國休戚，庇心之至，不敢不陳。

translations.literal: We your subjects hold office in our posts and share the state's weal and woe; to the utmost of sheltering heart we dare not fail to state it.
translations.idiomatic: We hold office in our posts and share the state's weal and woe; to the utmost of our devotion we dare not fail to speak.

sentences.zh: 咸以為天下之至尊，莫尊於王業；

translations.literal: All consider that of what is most honored under heaven nothing is more honored than the royal enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: All hold that of what is most honored under heaven nothing is more honored than the royal enterprise;

sentences.zh: 皇極之至重，莫重於萬機。

translations.literal: of what is most weighty at the imperial pole nothing is more weighty than the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and of what is most weighty at the imperial pole nothing is more weighty than the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 至尊，故不得以常禮任己；

translations.literal: Because of supreme honor one may not indulge oneself with ordinary ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Because of supreme honor one may not indulge oneself with ordinary ritual;

sentences.zh: 至重，亦弗獲以世典申情。

translations.literal: because of utmost weight one also cannot express feeling through worldly canon.
translations.idiomatic: and because of utmost weight one also cannot express feeling through worldly precedent alone.

sentences.zh: 是以二漢已降，逮于魏晉，葬不過踰月，服不淹三旬。

translations.literal: Therefore from the two Han down through Wei and Jin, burial did not exceed a month and mourning garments did not last three ten-day periods.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from the two Han down through Wei and Jin, burial did not exceed a month and mourning garments did not last thirty days.

sentences.zh: 良以叔世事廣，禮隨時變，不可以無為之法，行之於有為之辰。

translations.literal: Truly because in middle generations affairs were broad and ritual changed with the time—one cannot apply the method of non-action in a time of action.
translations.idiomatic: This is because in middle generations affairs were broad and ritual changed with the times—one cannot apply the method of non-action in a time that demands action.

sentences.zh: 文質不同，古今異制，其來久矣。

translations.literal: Refinement and simplicity differ; ancient and modern institutions differ—this has been so for long.
translations.idiomatic: Refinement and simplicity differ; ancient and modern institutions differ—this has been so for a long time.

sentences.zh: 自皇代革命，多歷年祀，四祖三宗，相繼纂業。

translations.literal: Since the imperial age's revolution many years and sacrifices have passed; four ancestors and three founders have succeeded one another in inheriting the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial dynasty's rise many years have passed; four ancestors and three founders have succeeded one another in inheriting the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 上承數代之故實，俯副兆民之企望，豈伊不懷，理宜然也。

translations.literal: Looking up they inherited the solid facts of many generations; looking down they answered the hopes of the hundred millions—how could they not cherish it? Reason demands that it be so.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up they inherited the solid facts of many generations; looking down they answered the hopes of the hundred millions—how could they not cherish it? Reason demands that it be so.

sentences.zh: 文明太皇太后欽明稽古，聖思淵深，所造終制，事合世典。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming was reverent, bright, and examined antiquity; her sage thought was profound and deep; the final regulations she created accorded with worldly canon.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming was reverent, bright, and examined antiquity; her sage thought was profound; the final regulations she created accorded with established precedent.

sentences.zh: 送終之禮既明，遺誥之文載備，奉而行之，足以垂風百王，軌儀萬葉。

translations.literal: The rites of seeing one to the end were already clear and the writings of her final commands fully complete; to receive and practice them is enough to hand down standards to a hundred kings and model ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of final send-off were already clear and the writings of her final commands fully complete; to receive and practice them is enough to hand down standards to a hundred kings and model ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至孝之誠，哀毀過禮，三御不充半溢，晝夜不釋絰帶，永思纏綿，滅性幾及。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with sincerity of utmost filial piety, grief and emaciation exceeding ritual—the three meals do not fill half a dipper, day and night you do not remove the hemp sash, eternal thought tangled and close, nearly reaching self-extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with sincerity of utmost filial piety, grief and emaciation exceeding ritual propriety—the three daily meals do not fill half a dipper, day and night you do not remove the hemp mourning sash, your eternal longing tangled and close, nearly reaching self-destruction.

sentences.zh: 百姓所以憂懼失守，臣等所以肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: This is why the common people are worried and fearful, losing their composure, and why we your subjects would lay our livers and brains on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the common people are worried and fearful, losing their composure, and why we would lay down our lives for you.

sentences.zh: 王者之尊，躬行一日，固可以感徹上靈，貫被幽顯。

translations.literal: The honor of the king—if he personally practices for one day, he can surely move and penetrate the upper spirits and extend through the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The honor of the king—if he personally practices for one day, he can surely move the upper spirits and extend through the hidden and manifest realms.

sentences.zh: 況今山陵告終，百禮咸畢，[1]日已淹月，仍不卜練，比之前世，理為過矣。

translations.literal: How much more now that the mountain tomb is announced complete and the hundred rites are all finished—days have already filled a month, yet you still do not select a day for the lian mourning; compared with former ages, by reason this is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now that the imperial tomb rites are complete and the hundred ceremonies finished—days have already filled a month, yet you still do not select a day for the lian mourning; compared with former ages, by reason this is excessive.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思大孝終始之義，愍億兆悲惶之心，抑思割哀，遵奉終制，以時即吉，一日萬機，則天下蒙恩，率土仰賴。

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to think on the meaning of great filial piety from beginning to end, pity the hundred millions' hearts of grief and fear, restrain thought and cut grief, follow and receive the final regulations, return to auspicious observance at the proper time, and handle ten thousand affairs in one day—then all under heaven would receive grace and the whole land would look up in reliance.
translations.idiomatic: We wish Your Majesty to reflect on the meaning of great filial piety from beginning to end, pity the hundred millions' hearts of grief and fear, restrain your grief, follow the final regulations, return to normal observance at the proper time, and handle the myriad affairs of state—then all under heaven would receive grace and the whole land would look up in reliance.

sentences.zh: 謹依前式，求定練日，以備祔禫之禮。」

translations.literal: We respectfully follow the former pattern and seek to fix the day of lian mourning to prepare the rites of fu-shan.'
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully follow the former pattern and seek to fix the day of lian mourning to prepare the rites of enshrinement and end of mourning.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「比當別敍在心。」

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Recently I shall separately set forth what is in my heart.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'I shall soon set forth separately what is in my heart.'

sentences.zh: 既而，帝引見太尉丕及羣臣等於太和殿前，哭拜盡哀，出幸思賢門右，詔尚書李沖宣旨於王等：「仰惟先后平日，近集羣官，共論政治，平秩民務。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Emperor summoned an audience with Grand Commandant Pi and the host of ministers before the Hall of Great Harmony, wept and bowed to the full measure of grief, went out to favor the right of the Gate of Cherishing the Worthy, and ordered Master of Writing Li Chong to proclaim the intent to the princes and others: 'Looking up I recall the Empress's ordinary days—recently she gathered officials and together discussed government, leveling and ordering the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Emperor summoned Grand Commandant Pi and the host of ministers before the Hall of Great Harmony, wept and bowed to the full measure of grief, went out to the right of the Gate of Cherishing the Worthy, and ordered Master of Writing Li Chong to proclaim his intent to the princes: 'Looking up I recall the Empress's ordinary days—recently she gathered officials and together discussed government, leveling and ordering the people's affairs.

sentences.zh: 何圖一旦禍酷奄鍾，獨見公卿，言及喪事，追惟荼毒，五內崩摧。」

translations.literal: Who could have thought that in a single morning disaster and cruelty would suddenly strike—now I alone see the dukes and ministers and speak of funeral matters; recalling the bitter poison, my five viscera collapse and are shattered.'
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought that in a single morning disaster would suddenly strike—now I alone see the dukes and ministers and speak of funeral matters; recalling the bitter anguish, my five viscera collapse and are shattered.'

sentences.zh: 丕對曰：「伏奉明詔，羣情圮絕。

translations.literal: Pi replied: 'We humbly receive the clear edict; the host's feelings are destroyed and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Pi replied: 'We humbly receive your clear edict; the feelings of all are destroyed and cut off.

sentences.zh: 臣與元等不識古義，以老朽之年，歷奉累聖，國家舊事，頗所知聞。

translations.literal: I and Yuan and the others do not understand ancient meaning; in our decrepit old age we have served successive sage emperors and have heard quite a bit of the state's former affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and I do not understand ancient meaning; in our decrepit old age we have served successive sage emperors and have heard quite a bit of the state's former affairs.

sentences.zh: 伏惟遠祖重光世襲，至有大諱之日，唯侍送梓宮者凶服，左右盡皆從吉。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that from remote ancestors through repeated glory and hereditary succession, down to the day of great taboo, only those attending and escorting the spirit coffin wore mourning garments; those at left and right all followed auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that from remote ancestors through repeated glory and hereditary succession, down to the day of great taboo, only those attending and escorting the spirit coffin wore mourning garments; everyone else at left and right followed auspicious observance.

sentences.zh: 四祖三宗，因而無改。

translations.literal: The four ancestors and three founders followed this without change.
translations.idiomatic: The four ancestors and three founders followed this without change.

sentences.zh: 世祖、高宗臣所目見。

translations.literal: Shizu and Gaozong I witnessed with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu and Gaozong I witnessed with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 唯先帝升遐，臣受任長安，不在侍送之列，竊聞所傳，無異前式。

translations.literal: Only when the former Emperor ascended to the distant realm I received appointment at Chang'an and was not in the ranks of those attending the escort; I privately heard what was transmitted and it did not differ from the former pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the former Emperor passed away I received appointment at Chang'an and was not in the ranks of those attending the escort; I privately heard what was transmitted and it did not differ from the former pattern.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以至孝之性，哀毀過禮，伏聞所御三食，不滿半溢。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, with a nature of utmost filial piety, grief and emaciation exceeding ritual—we humbly hear that the three meals you take do not fill half a dipper.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly note that Your Majesty, with a nature of utmost filial piety, grief and emaciation exceeding ritual propriety—we humbly hear that the three meals you take do not fill half a dipper.

sentences.zh: 臣等叩心絕氣，坐不安席。

translations.literal: We your subjects knock our hearts and stop our breath; we cannot sit at ease on our mats.
translations.idiomatic: We knock our hearts and stop our breath; we cannot sit at ease on our mats.

sentences.zh: 願暫抑至慕之情，遵先朝成事，思金冊遺令，奉行前式，無失舊典。」

translations.literal: We wish you temporarily to restrain the feeling of utmost longing, follow the former court's accomplished affairs, reflect on the golden book's final commands, receive and practice the former pattern, and not lose the old canon.'
translations.idiomatic: We wish you temporarily to restrain your utmost longing, follow the former court's accomplished precedents, reflect on the golden book's final commands, practice the former pattern, and not lose the old canon.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「追惟慈恩，昊天罔極，哀毀常事，豈足關言。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Recalling maternal grace—vast Heaven is without limit; grief and emaciation are ordinary matters—how could they be worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'Recalling maternal grace—vast Heaven is without limit; grief and emaciation are ordinary matters—how could they be worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 既不能待沒，而朝夕食粥，粗亦支任，二公何足以至憂怖。

translations.literal: Since I could not wait until her death, morning and evening I eat gruel and can roughly sustain myself—how could the two dukes be so worried and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Since I could not wait until her death, morning and evening I eat gruel and can roughly sustain myself—why should the two dukes be so worried and fearful.

sentences.zh: 所奏先朝成事，亦所見聞。

translations.literal: What you submit about the former court's accomplished affairs I also have seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: What you submit about the former court's accomplished affairs I also have seen and heard.

sentences.zh: 祖宗情專武略，未修文教。

translations.literal: The ancestors and founders focused their feeling on military strategy and did not cultivate literary teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors and founders focused on military strategy and did not cultivate literary teaching.

sentences.zh: 朕今仰禀聖訓，庶習古道，論時比事，又與先世不同。

translations.literal: I now look up and receive the sage's instruction, hoping to study the ancient way—discussing the time and comparing affairs, it again differs from the former age.
translations.idiomatic: I now look up and receive the sage's instruction, hoping to study the ancient way—discussing the time and comparing affairs, it again differs from the former age.

sentences.zh: 太尉等國老，政之所寄，於典記舊式，或所未悉，且可知朕大意。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant and others are elders of the state on whom government is entrusted; regarding canonical records and old patterns they may not all be familiar—yet you may know my general intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant and the others are elders of the state on whom government is entrusted; regarding canonical records and old patterns they may not all be familiar—yet you may know my general intent.

sentences.zh: 其餘喪禮之儀，古今異同，漢魏成事及先儒所論，朕雖在衰服之中，以喪禮事重，情在必行，故暫抑哀慕，躬自尋覽。

translations.literal: As for the remaining rites of mourning ritual, ancient and modern similarities and differences, Han and Wei accomplished affairs and what former Confucians discussed—although I am within mourning garments, because mourning ritual affairs are weighty and feeling must be carried through, I therefore temporarily restrain longing and grief and personally search and review.
translations.idiomatic: As for the remaining rites of mourning, ancient and modern similarities and differences, Han and Wei precedents and what former Confucians discussed—although I am in mourning garments, because mourning ritual affairs are weighty and feeling must be carried through, I therefore temporarily restrain my longing and grief and personally search and review them.

sentences.zh: 今且以所懷，別問尚書游明根、高閭等，公且可聽之。」

translations.literal: For now I shall take what is in my heart and separately question Masters of Writing You Minggen, Gao Lu, and others—you may listen for now.'
translations.idiomatic: For now I shall take what is in my heart and separately question Masters of Writing You Minggen, Gao Lu, and others—you may listen for now.'

sentences.zh: 高祖謂明根曰：「朕丁罹酷罰，日月推移，山陵已過，公卿又依金冊，據案魏晉，請除衰服。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Minggen: 'I have encountered cruel punishment; sun and moon move on; the mountain tomb has passed; the dukes and ministers again rely on the golden book, cite Wei and Jin cases, and request removal of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said to Minggen: 'I have encountered cruel punishment; the days pass; the imperial tomb rites are complete; the dukes and ministers again rely on the golden book, cite Wei and Jin precedents, and request that I remove my mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 重聞所奏，倍增號哽。

translations.literal: Hearing again what they submit, my choked cries of grief are doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing again what they submit, my choked cries of grief are doubled.

sentences.zh: 前者事逼山陵，哀疚頓弊，未得論敍，今故相引，欲具通所懷。

translations.literal: Earlier affairs pressed upon the mountain tomb; grief and affliction were suddenly exhausted and I could not discuss and set forth; now I therefore draw you in, wishing fully to communicate what is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier affairs pressed upon the imperial tomb; grief and affliction overwhelmed me and I could not set forth my views; now I therefore draw you in, wishing fully to communicate what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 卿前所表，除釋衰麻，聞之實用悲恨。

translations.literal: Your former memorial removing and releasing coarse hemp—I heard it and truly felt grief and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Your former memorial on removing coarse hemp mourning—I heard it and truly felt grief and anguish.

sentences.zh: 于時親侍梓宮，匍匐筵几，哀號痛慕，情未暫闋，而公卿何忍便有此言。

translations.literal: At that time I personally attended the spirit coffin, crawling on the mat and table, crying in grief and painful longing—feeling had not briefly ceased—how could the dukes and ministers bear to speak such words at once?
translations.idiomatic: At that time I personally attended the spirit coffin, prostrate on the mat and table, crying in grief and painful longing—my feeling had not briefly ceased—how could the dukes and ministers bear to speak such words at once?

sentences.zh: 何於人情之不足！

translations.literal: How lacking in human feeling!
translations.idiomatic: How lacking in human feeling!

sentences.zh: 夫聖人制卒哭之禮，授練之變，皆奪情以漸。

translations.literal: The sage established the rite of ending wailing and the change of granting lian—all restrain feeling by gradual steps.
translations.idiomatic: The sage established the rite of ending wailing and the change of granting lian—all restrain feeling by gradual steps.

sentences.zh: 又聞君子不奪人之喪，亦不可奪喪。

translations.literal: I also hear that the gentleman does not seize another's mourning, nor may mourning be seized from one.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that the gentleman does not cut short another's mourning, nor may one's mourning be cut short.

sentences.zh: 今則旬日之間，言及即吉，特成傷理。」

translations.literal: Now within a ten-day period they speak of at once returning to auspicious observance—this especially becomes injury to principle.'
translations.idiomatic: Now within a ten-day period they speak of at once returning to normal observance—this especially violates principle.'

sentences.zh: 明根對曰：「臣等伏尋金冊遺旨，踰月而葬，葬而即吉。

translations.literal: Minggen replied: 'We your subjects humbly trace the golden book's final intent—bury after a month, and after burial at once return to auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen replied: 'We humbly trace the golden book's final intent—bury after a month, and after burial at once return to normal observance.

sentences.zh: 故於卜葬之初，因奏練除之事，仰傷聖心，伏增悲悚。」

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of selecting the burial day we took occasion to submit the matter of lian removal—looking up we wounded the sage heart; humbly our grief and fear increased.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the beginning of selecting the burial day we took occasion to submit the matter of lian removal—looking up we wounded your sage heart; humbly our grief and fear increased.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿等咸稱三年之喪，雖則自古，然中代以後，未之能行。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You all uniformly say three-year mourning, though ancient, yet since the middle ages it has not been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You all say three-year mourning, though ancient, yet since the middle ages it has not been practiced.

sentences.zh: 朕謂中代所以不遂三年之喪，蓋由君上違世，繼主初立，故身襲衮冕，以行即位之禮。

translations.literal: I consider that the reason the middle ages did not carry through three-year mourning is broadly because when the ruler above departed the world the succeeding lord was newly established, so he personally assumed dragon robes and dragon cap to perform the rites of accession.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that the reason the middle ages did not carry through three-year mourning is broadly because when the ruler departed the world the succeeding lord was newly established, so he personally assumed dragon robes and cap to perform the rites of accession.

sentences.zh: 又從儲宮而登極者，君德未沇，臣義不洽，天下顒顒，未知所傒，故頒備朝儀，示皇極之尊。

translations.literal: Moreover for one who ascended the ultimate from the heir apparent—the ruler's virtue was not yet settled, ministers' righteousness not yet harmonized, all under heaven looked up expectantly not knowing what to hope for—therefore he promulgated complete court ritual to display the honor of the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover for one who ascended the throne from the heir apparent—the ruler's virtue was not yet settled, ministers' righteousness not yet harmonized, all under heaven looked up expectantly not knowing what to hope for—therefore he promulgated complete court ritual to display the honor of the imperial pole.

sentences.zh: 及后之喪也，因父在不遂，即生惰易之情，踵以為法。

translations.literal: As for mourning for the empress, because the father was alive it was not carried through, and at once the feeling of lax ease arose and was followed as law.
translations.idiomatic: As for mourning for the empress, because the father was alive it was not carried through, and at once the feeling of lax ease arose and was followed as law.

sentences.zh: 諒知敦厚之化，不易遵也。

translations.literal: They understood that the transformation of deep generosity is not easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: They knew that the full measure of sincere mourning was hard to follow.

sentences.zh: 朕少蒙鞠育，慈嚴兼至，臣子之情，君父之道，無不備誨。

translations.literal: I from youth received nurturing upbringing; kindness and severity both reached their utmost; the feelings of subject and minister, the way of ruler and father—none were not fully instructed.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood I was nourished in her care; kindness and discipline alike reached their fullest; as subject and son, as ruler and father, nothing in that bond was left untaught.

sentences.zh: 雖自蒙昧，粗解告旨，庶望量行，以免咎戾。

translations.literal: Though I am myself ignorant and dim, I roughly understand what was told and enjoined, and hope to measure my conduct thereby to avoid blame and offense.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am myself unlearned, I roughly grasp her admonitions and hope to act accordingly, that I may avoid fault and offense.

sentences.zh: 朕誠不德，在位過紀，雖未能恩洽四方，化行萬國，仰稟聖訓，足令億兆知有君矣。

translations.literal: I truly lack virtue; on the throne I have passed a cycle of years; though I could not extend grace to all four quarters or spread transformation to ten thousand states, receiving upward the sage instruction suffices to make the hundred millions know there is a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I truly lack virtue; I have reigned more than a full cycle of years; though I could not extend grace to all four quarters or spread transformation throughout the realm, upheld by her sage instruction the hundred millions yet know there is a ruler.

sentences.zh: 於此之日，而不遂哀慕之心，使情禮俱損，喪紀圮壞者，深可痛恨。」

translations.literal: On such a day as this, yet not to fulfill the heart of grieving longing, causing feeling and ritual both to be injured and mourning statutes to collapse—this is deeply to be hated and regretted.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet on such a day as this not to fulfill my heart of grief and longing, to let both feeling and ritual suffer and the mourning statutes crumble—this is deeply to be lamented.'

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「太古既遠，事難襲用，漢魏以來，據有成事。

translations.literal: Gao Lu replied: 'High antiquity is already distant; affairs are hard to inherit and apply; since Han and Wei, one may rely on established precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: 'High antiquity is already distant; its practices are hard to adopt wholesale; since Han and Wei one may rely on established precedents.

sentences.zh: 漢文繼高惠之蹤，斷獄四百，幾致刑措，猶垂三旬之禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han continued the tracks of Gaozu and Empress Dowager Hui; cases judged were four hundred, almost reaching the point of punishments set aside, yet he still observed the thirty-day rite.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han followed Gaozu and Empress Dowager Hui; only four hundred cases were tried, punishments nearly fell into disuse, yet he still observed the thirty-day mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 孝景承平，遵而不變。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing inherited peace and followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing inherited a time of peace and followed without change.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，不為即位之際，有所逼懼也。

translations.literal: Spoken from this, it was not that at the moment of accession there was some compulsion or fear.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that they were not acting at accession under compulsion or fear.

sentences.zh: 良是君人之道，理自宜然。

translations.literal: Truly this is the way of a ruler; principle from itself is fitting so.
translations.idiomatic: Truly this is the way of a ruler; by principle it was fitting so.

sentences.zh: 又漢稱文景，雖非聖君，亦中代明主。

translations.literal: Moreover Han calls them Wen and Jing; though not sage rulers, they were yet enlightened lords of the middle age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han praises Wen and Jing; though not sage rulers, they were enlightened sovereigns of the middle age.

sentences.zh: 今遺冊之旨，同於前式。

translations.literal: Now the intent of the testamentary book is the same as the former pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Now the testamentary book's intent matches the former pattern.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下述遵遺令，以副羣庶之情。

translations.literal: Humbly we wish Your Majesty to narrate and follow the final command, to accord with the feelings of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty to follow the final command and satisfy the feelings of the people.

sentences.zh: 杜預晉之碩學，論自古天子無有行三年之喪者，以為漢文之制，闇與古合。

translations.literal: Du Yu was Jin's great scholar; he discussed that from antiquity no Son of Heaven had practiced three-year mourning, holding that Emperor Wen's institution darkly agreed with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu was Jin's leading scholar; he argued that from antiquity no Son of Heaven had observed three-year mourning, and held that Emperor Wen's practice tacitly accorded with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 雖叔世所行，事可承踵，是以臣等慺慺干謁。」

translations.literal: Though what the declining age practiced, the matter may be inherited and followed; therefore we your subjects earnestly and repeatedly present ourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Though it was the practice of a declining age, the precedent may still be followed; therefore we earnestly press our petition.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「漢魏之事，與今不同，備如向說。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Han and Wei affairs differ from today; fully as just said.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Han and Wei affairs differ from today, as I have just explained in full.

sentences.zh: 孝景雖承昇平之基，然由嫡子即位，君德未顯，無異前古。

translations.literal: Xiaojing though inherited a foundation of rising peace, yet by the legitimate son ascending the throne, the ruler's virtue was not yet displayed—no different from ancient times before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojing though inherited a foundation of rising peace, ascended as the legitimate heir while his virtue was not yet manifest—no different from earlier times.

sentences.zh: 又父子之親，誠是天屬之重，然聖母之德，昊天莫報，思自殞滅，豈從衰服而已。

translations.literal: Moreover the closeness of father and son is truly the weight of heaven's kin; yet the sage mother's virtue—broad heaven cannot repay; thinking to destroy oneself, how could it be merely following coarse mourning garments?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the bond of father and son is truly heaven's closest tie; yet the sage mother's virtue—broad heaven cannot repay it; the thought is to give up one's life—how could that be satisfied by coarse mourning garments alone?

sentences.zh: 竊尋金冊之旨，所以告奪臣子之心令早即吉者，慮遺絕萬機，荒廢政事。

translations.literal: I privately trace the golden book's intent: the reason for instructing to seize the hearts of ministers and subjects and order early return to auspicious observance is concern lest the myriad affairs be left behind and government business be left waste.
translations.idiomatic: I privately trace the golden book's intent: it instructs ministers and subjects to set grief aside and return early to normal observance lest the myriad affairs be neglected and government fall into neglect.

sentences.zh: 羣官所以慺慺，亦懼機務之不理矣。

translations.literal: The reason the multitude of officials are earnest and repeated is also fear that urgent business will not be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The reason officials press so earnestly is also fear that urgent business will go unattended.

sentences.zh: 今仰奉冊令，俯順羣心，不敢闇默不言，以荒庶政。

translations.literal: Now looking up I receive the book's command; looking down I comply with the multitude's hearts—I dare not be darkly silent and not speak, thereby leaving common government waste.
translations.idiomatic: Now I receive the book's command from above and comply with the officials' wishes below; I dare not remain silent and leave government affairs neglected.

sentences.zh: 唯欲存衰麻，廢吉禮，朔望盡哀，寫泄悲慕，上無失導誨之志，下不乖眾官所請，情在可許，故專欲行之。

translations.literal: Only I wish to preserve coarse hemp, abolish auspicious ritual; on new moon and full moon exhaust grief, pour forth grief and longing; above not losing the will of guiding instruction, below not going against what the multitude of officials request—feeling lies where it may be permitted, therefore I alone wish to carry it through.
translations.idiomatic: I only wish to keep coarse hemp mourning, set aside auspicious ritual, grieve fully at each new and full moon, and pour out my grief; above, not failing her guiding instruction, below, not going against what officials request—where feeling may be permitted, I therefore insist on doing so.

sentences.zh: 公卿宜審思朕懷，不當固執。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers should carefully consider what is in my breast and ought not obstinately cling.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers should weigh what is in my heart and ought not cling obstinately to their view.

sentences.zh: 至如杜預之論，雖暫適時事，於孺慕之君，諒闇之主，蓋亦誣矣。

translations.literal: As for Du Yu's discussion—though for the moment it fits current affairs—for a lord still in childlike longing mourning, a ruler still in the dark of mourning, it is probably also slander.
translations.idiomatic: As for Du Yu's argument—though for the moment it fits current affairs—for a ruler still in childlike grief, still in the darkness of mourning, it is surely wide of the mark.

sentences.zh: 孔聖稱『喪與其易也寧戚』，而預於孝道簡略，朕無取焉。」

translations.literal: The sage Confucius said 'mourning—with its ease rather its grief'; yet Yu toward filial piety was brief and simple—I have nothing to take from him.'
translations.idiomatic: The sage Confucius said, 'In mourning, better genuine grief than an easy observance,' yet Yu treated filial piety as something brief and simple—I have nothing to take from him.'

sentences.zh: 祕書丞李彪對曰：「漢明德馬后，保養章帝，母子之道，無可間然。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao replied: 'In Han, the illumined virtue Empress Ma raised and nurtured Emperor Zhang; the way of mother and son—nothing could come between.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Biao replied: 'In Han, the Illumined Virtue Empress Ma raised and nurtured Emperor Zhang; the bond of mother and son admitted no breach.

sentences.zh: 及后之崩，葬不淹旬，尋以從吉。

translations.literal: When the empress died, burial did not exceed ten days; soon thereafter he followed auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died, burial came within ten days, and soon thereafter he returned to normal observance.

sentences.zh: 然漢章不受譏於前代，明德不損名於往史。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Zhang of Han received no censure from former ages, and Illumined Virtue did not diminish her name in past histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Zhang incurred no censure from former ages, and Illumined Virtue did not lose standing in past histories.

sentences.zh: 雖論功比德，事有殊絕，然母子之親，抑亦可擬。

translations.literal: Though comparing merit and comparing virtue the matter has extremes of difference, yet the closeness of mother and son may yet be likened.
translations.idiomatic: Though merit and virtue differ beyond comparison, the bond of mother and son may yet be likened.

sentences.zh: 願陛下覽前世之成規，遵金冊之遺令，割哀從議，以親萬機。

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to review former ages' established rules, follow the golden book's final command, cut grief and follow counsel, to attend personally to the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to review former precedents, follow the golden book's final command, set grief aside and accept our counsel, and attend personally to the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 斯誠臣下至心，兆庶所願。」

translations.literal: This truly is the inmost heart of your subjects below, what the hundred millions desire.'
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the inmost wish of your subjects and of the hundred millions.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「既言事殊，固不宜仰匹至德，復稱孝章從吉，不受譏前代。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Having already said the affairs differ, it surely is not fitting to look up and match ultimate virtue; again citing Xiaozhang following auspicious observance and not receiving censure from former ages—
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Having already said the cases differ, it is surely not fitting to look up and match ultimate virtue, then again cite Emperor Zhang's return to normal observance and freedom from censure in former ages—

sentences.zh: 朕所以眷戀衰絰，不從所議者，仰感慈恩，情不能忍故也。

translations.literal: The reason I linger on coarse mourning fringe and do not follow what was discussed is looking up I feel kind grace—feeling cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I cling to coarse mourning fringe and do not follow your counsel is that, looking up, I feel her kind grace and my heart cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞孝子之居喪，見美麗則感親，故釋錦而服粗衰。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the filial son dwells in mourning, seeing beauty he is moved regarding his parent; therefore he releases brocade and wears coarse mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a filial son is in mourning, seeing beauty reminds him of his parent; therefore he puts aside brocade and wears coarse hemp.

sentences.zh: 內外相稱，非虛加也。

translations.literal: Inner and outer mutually correspond—it is not vain addition.
translations.idiomatic: Inner feeling and outward display correspond; it is not mere show.

sentences.zh: 今者豈徒顧禮違議，苟免嗤嫌而已。

translations.literal: Now is it merely attending to ritual and violating discussion, perfunctorily avoiding ridicule and dislike?
translations.idiomatic: Surely I am not merely attending to ritual, defying your counsel, and seeking only to avoid ridicule?

sentences.zh: 抑亦情發於衷，而欲肆之於外。

translations.literal: Rather feeling issues from within the breast and I wish to give it free rein outward.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, feeling rises from within and I wish to give it outward expression.

sentences.zh: 金冊之意，已具前答，故不復重論。

translations.literal: The golden book's meaning has already been fully answered before; therefore I do not again repeat the discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The golden book's meaning I have already answered fully; I will not repeat the argument.

sentences.zh: 又卒日奉旨，不忍片言。

translations.literal: Moreover on the day of [her] passing I received the directive and could not bear a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the day of her passing I received your directive and could not bear a single word in reply.

sentences.zh: 後事遂非，默默在念，不顯所懷。

translations.literal: Later affairs accordingly went wrong; silently it remained in thought, not displaying what was in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Later matters went awry; I kept my thoughts to myself and did not reveal what was in my heart.

sentences.zh: 今奉終之事，一以仰遵遺冊，於令不敢有乖。

translations.literal: Now regarding final matters I uniformly look up and follow the testamentary book—in the command I dare not have any deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in funeral matters, I uniformly follow the testamentary book; in what it commands I dare not deviate.

sentences.zh: 但痛慕之心，事繫於予。

translations.literal: Only the heart of painful longing—the matter binds to me.
translations.idiomatic: Only the heart of painful longing is a matter that binds to me alone.

sentences.zh: 雖無丁蘭之感，庶聖靈不奪至願，是以謂無違旨嫌。

translations.literal: Though without Ding Lan's feeling, I hope the sage spirit will not seize my utmost wish; therefore I say there is no suspicion of violating the directive.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack Ding Lan's devotion, I hope her sage spirit will not deny my utmost wish; therefore I say there is no ground to suspect violation of her command.

sentences.zh: 諸公所表，稱先朝成式，事在可準。

translations.literal: What the lords submitted states former dynasty's established patterns—the matter lies where it may be taken as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial cites former dynasties' established patterns as something that may serve as standard.

sentences.zh: 朕仰惟太祖龍飛九五，初定中原，及太宗承基，世祖纂歷，皆以四方未一，羣雄競起，故銳意武功，未修文德。

translations.literal: I look up and reflect: Taizu dragon-flew to the nine and five, at first settled the Central Plain; and Taizong inherited the foundation, Shizu continued the register—all because the four quarters were not yet one and rival heroes rose competing; therefore they sharpened intent on martial achievement and did not cultivate civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that Taizu rose to the throne, first settled the Central Plain, and Taizong and Shizu in turn inherited and continued the line—all while the four quarters were not yet united and rival heroes contended; therefore they focused on martial achievement and did not cultivate civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 高宗、顯祖亦心存武烈，因循無改。

translations.literal: Gaozong and Xianzu also kept martial splendor in mind and followed along without change.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and Xianzu likewise kept martial glory in mind and followed precedent without change.

sentences.zh: 朕承累世之資，仰聖善之訓，撫和內外，上下輯諧。

translations.literal: I inherit accumulated generations' resources, receive upward the sage-good instruction, soothe and harmonize inner and outer, above and below unite in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: I inherit the accumulated resources of many reigns and receive her sage and good instruction; I have soothed and harmonized inner and outer, and above and below are united.

sentences.zh: 稽參古式，憲章舊典，四海移風，要荒革俗。

translations.literal: I examine and consult ancient patterns, take as charter old canons; within the four seas customs shift, at the frontier wastes customs are reformed.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined ancient models and taken old canons as charter; within the four seas customs have shifted, and even the frontier wastes have changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 仰遵明軌，庶無愆違。

translations.literal: Looking up I follow the enlightened track, hoping without offense or deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up, I follow the enlightened path, hoping to commit no offense or deviation.

sentences.zh: 而方於禍酷之辰，引末朝因循之則，以為前準，非是所喻。」

translations.literal: Yet just at a time of calamity and cruelty to cite the last dynasty's follow-along rules as former standard—this is not what may be explained.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet at a time of such calamity to cite the last dynasty's follow-along rules as precedent—this is not what I can accept.'

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「臣等以先朝所行，頗同魏晉，又適於時，故敢仍請。」

translations.literal: Gao Lu replied: 'We your subjects hold that what former dynasties practiced is rather the same as Wei and Jin, and again fits the time; therefore we dare again to request.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: 'We hold that what former dynasties practiced largely matches Wei and Jin, and again fits the times; therefore we dare press our request again.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿等又稱今雖中夏穆清，庶邦康靜，然萬機事廣，不可暫曠。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You again say that though today the central Xia is clear and pure and the numerous states are tranquil and quiet, yet the myriad affairs are extensive and cannot briefly be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You again say that though the central realm is tranquil and the myriad states at peace, the affairs of state are vast and cannot be left vacant even briefly.

sentences.zh: 朕以卿苦見逼奪，情不自勝。

translations.literal: I because you bitterly appear to force and seize—feeling cannot overcome itself.
translations.idiomatic: Because you press me so bitterly, my feelings cannot contain themselves.

sentences.zh: 尋覽喪儀，見前賢論者，稱卒哭之後，王者得理庶事。

translations.literal: Searching through mourning ritual I see former worthies who discussed say that after ending wailing the king may order common affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Searching through mourning ritual, I find former worthies who say that after the end of wailing a king may attend to common affairs.

sentences.zh: 依據此文，又從遺冊之旨，雖存衰服，不廢萬機，無闕庶政，得展罔極之思，於情差申。」

translations.literal: Relying on this text, and again following the testament's intent—though preserving mourning garments, not abolishing the myriad affairs, without lack in common government, able to extend unfathomable longing—in feeling it is somewhat fulfilled.'
translations.idiomatic: Relying on this text and again following the testament's intent, I may keep mourning garments yet not abandon the myriad affairs, leave government unimpaired, and still extend my boundless longing—in feeling this is somewhat fulfilled.'

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「君不除服於上，臣則釋衰於下，從服之義有違，為臣之道不足。

translations.literal: Gao Lu replied: 'If the ruler does not remove garments above, ministers then release mourning below—the meaning of following mourning is violated; the way of serving as minister is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: 'If the ruler does not remove mourning above, ministers release mourning below—the principle of shared mourning is violated and the minister's duty is unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 又親御衰麻，復聽朝政，吉凶事雜，臣竊為疑。」

translations.literal: Moreover personally wearing coarse hemp yet again hearing court government—auspicious and inauspicious affairs intermixed—I privately have doubt.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to wear mourning garments personally yet again hear court government, with auspicious and inauspicious affairs intermixed—I privately have doubts.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿等猶以朕之未除於上，不忍專釋於下，奈何令朕獨忍於親舊！

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You still because I have not removed mourning above cannot bear to release mourning alone below—how can you make me alone bear it among kin and old associates!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'You still, because I have not removed mourning above, cannot bear to release mourning below—how then can you make me bear mourning alone among kin and old associates!

sentences.zh: 論云，王者不遂三年之服者，屈己以寬羣下也。

translations.literal: Discussions say: the king who does not carry through three-year garments restrains himself to widen those below.
translations.idiomatic: Discussions say that a king who does not observe three-year mourning restrains himself to give latitude to those below.

sentences.zh: 先后之撫羣下也，念之若子，視之猶傷。

translations.literal: The late empress in soothing those below thought of them as sons and viewed them as still wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The late empress in caring for those below thought of them as sons and viewed them as still wounded.

sentences.zh: 卿等哀慕之思，既不求寬；

translations.literal: Your grief-longing thoughts do not seek widening;
translations.idiomatic: Your thoughts of grief and longing do not seek such latitude;

sentences.zh: 朕欲盡罔極之慕，何為不可？

translations.literal: I wish to exhaust unfathomable longing—why may it not be?
translations.idiomatic: why may I not exhaust my boundless longing?

sentences.zh: 但逼遺冊，不遂乃心。

translations.literal: Only compelled by the testamentary book, my own heart is not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I am only compelled by the testamentary book, and my own heart is not fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 將欲居廬服衰，寫朝夕之慕；

translations.literal: I am about to dwell in a hut and wear mourning, pouring forth morning-and-evening longing;
translations.idiomatic: I intend to dwell in a mourning hut and wear coarse garments, pouring out morning-and-evening longing;

sentences.zh: 升堂襲素，理日昃之勤。

translations.literal: ascending the hall and assuming white garments, ordering the diligence of late afternoon.
translations.idiomatic: then ascend the hall in white garments and attend to the day's business at its height.

sentences.zh: 使大政不荒，哀情獲遂，吉不害於凶，凶無妨於吉。

translations.literal: Let great government not lie waste, grieving feeling obtain fulfillment—auspicious not harming inauspicious, inauspicious not obstructing auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Thus great government will not lie waste, grieving feeling may be fulfilled, and the auspicious will not harm the inauspicious nor the inauspicious obstruct the auspicious.

sentences.zh: 以心處之，謂為可爾。

translations.literal: Taking the heart to place it so—I say it can be so.
translations.idiomatic: Taking this to heart, I say it can be done.

sentences.zh: 遺旨之文，公卿所議，皆服終三旬，釋衰襲吉。

translations.literal: The testamentary text and what dukes and ministers discussed—all wear mourning to the end of thirty days, release mourning and assume auspicious garments.
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary text and what dukes and ministers discussed both prescribe mourning to the end of thirty days, then release mourning and assume auspicious garments.

sentences.zh: 從此而行，情實未忍；

translations.literal: Following this and acting—feeling truly cannot bear it;
translations.idiomatic: To follow that course my feeling truly cannot bear it;

sentences.zh: 遂服三年，重違旨誥。

translations.literal: then wearing three years heavily violates the directive edict.
translations.idiomatic: to wear mourning three years would gravely violate her directive edict.

sentences.zh: 今處二理之際，唯望至期，使四氣一周，寒暑代易。

translations.literal: Now situated at the border of two principles, I only hope for the full term, to let the four seasons complete one cycle and cold and heat alternate in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Now caught between two principles, I only hope for the full term, that the four seasons complete one cycle and cold and heat succeed one another.

sentences.zh: 雖不盡三年之心，得一經忌日，情結差申。

translations.literal: Though not exhausting the three-year heart, obtaining one passage through the anniversary of death, the knot of feeling is somewhat released.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot fulfill the three-year heart, to pass one anniversary of her death would somewhat ease the knot of feeling.

sentences.zh: 案禮，卒哭之後，將受變服。

translations.literal: According to ritual, after ending wailing one is about to receive changed garments.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, after the end of wailing one is about to receive changed garments.

sentences.zh: 於朕受日，庶民及小官皆命即吉。

translations.literal: On the day I receive [lian], common people and minor officials are all ordered at once to auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: On the day I receive lian garments, common people and minor officials are all ordered at once to normal observance.

sentences.zh: 內職羽林中郎已下，虎賁郎已上，及外職五品已上無衰服者，素服以終三月；

translations.literal: Inner offices from Household Guard Gentleman rank down, Tiger Guard Gentlemen rank up, and outer offices fifth rank and up without mourning garments—white garments to the end of three months;
translations.idiomatic: For inner offices from Household Guard Gentleman down and Tiger Guard Gentleman up, and for outer offices of fifth rank and above who wear no mourning garments, white garments until the end of three months;

sentences.zh: 內職及外臣衰服者，變從練禮。

translations.literal: inner offices and outer ministers wearing mourning garments change and follow lian ritual.
translations.idiomatic: inner offices and outer ministers in mourning garments shall change and follow lian ritual.

sentences.zh: 外臣三月而除；

translations.literal: Outer ministers remove mourning after three months;
translations.idiomatic: Outer ministers remove mourning after three months;

sentences.zh: 諸王、三都、駙馬及內職，至來年三月晦朕之練也，除凶即吉；

translations.literal: all princes, the three capitals, consorts of imperial daughters, and inner offices—until the last day of the third month of next year, my lian—remove inauspicious and assume auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: all princes, the three capitals, imperial sons-in-law, and inner offices—until the last day of the third month of next year, my lian observance—shall remove inauspicious garments and assume auspicious ones;

sentences.zh: 侍臣君服斯服，隨朕所降。

translations.literal: attending ministers, whatever garment the ruler wears that garment, following what I lower.
translations.idiomatic: attending ministers shall wear what the ruler wears, following what I prescribe.

sentences.zh: 此雖非舊式，推情即理，有貴賤之差，遠近之別。」

translations.literal: This though not the old pattern, pushing feeling accords with principle—there are differences of noble and base, near and far.'
translations.idiomatic: This is not the old pattern, but guided by feeling it accords with principle; there are differences of rank and of near and far.'

sentences.zh: 明根對曰：「聖慕深遠，孝情彌至，臣等所奏，已不蒙許，願得踰年即吉。

translations.literal: Minggen replied: 'Sage longing is deep and far; filial feeling is utmost. What we submitted already did not receive permission. We wish to obtain passing the year and at once auspicious observance.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen replied: 'Your sage grief is deep and far-reaching; your filial feeling is utmost. Our memorial has not been granted. We beg that after the year has passed you may at once return to normal observance.

sentences.zh: 既歷冬正，歲序改易，且足申至慕之情，又近遺誥之意，何待期年。」

translations.literal: Having already passed the winter solstice, the year's sequence has changed—moreover sufficient to express utmost longing feeling, and again near the testamentary edict's intent—why wait the full year.'
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice has passed and the year's sequence has changed; that is enough to express your utmost longing, and it is again near the testamentary edict's intent—why wait the full year?'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「冊旨速除之意，慮廣及百官，久曠眾務。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'The book's intent of swift removal is concern that it extend broadly to the hundred officials and long leave the multitude of duties vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'The book's intent in prescribing swift removal of mourning is concern that it extend broadly to the hundred officials and long leave public duties vacant.

sentences.zh: 豈於朕一人，獨有違奪？

translations.literal: How could it be for me alone that there is exclusive violation and seizure?
translations.idiomatic: How could it apply to me alone, with a special exception?

sentences.zh: 今既依次降除，各不廢王政，復何妨於事，而猶奪期年之心。」

translations.literal: Now having already in order lowered and removed mourning, each not abolishing royal government—what further impediment in affairs, yet still seizing the full-year heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that mourning has been lowered step by step and government is not suspended, what further impediment remains, that you still seek to seize my wish for the full year?'

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「昔王孫裸葬，士安去棺，其子皆從而不違，不為不孝。

translations.literal: Gao Lu replied: 'Formerly Wang Sun had naked burial and Shi'an removed the coffin; their sons all followed and did not violate it—not considered unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu replied: 'Formerly Wang Sun ordered naked burial and Shi'an removed his coffin; their sons all followed without violation and were not deemed unfilial.

sentences.zh: 此雖貴賤非倫，事頗相似，臣敢借以為諭。

translations.literal: This though noble and base are not of the same category, the affair is rather similar; I dare borrow it as illustration.
translations.idiomatic: Though rank differs, the cases are rather alike; I dare borrow them as illustration.

sentences.zh: 今親奉遺令，而有所不從，臣等所以頻煩干奏。」

translations.literal: Now personally receiving the final command yet in some matters not following—this is why we repeatedly and tediously present memorials.'
translations.idiomatic: Now we personally receive her final command, yet in some matters it is not followed—that is why we press our memorials again and again.'

sentences.zh: 李彪亦曰：「三年不改其父之道，可謂大孝。

translations.literal: Li Biao also said: 'Three years without changing his father's way—may be called great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao also said: 'Three years without changing his father's way may be called great filial piety.

sentences.zh: 今不遵冊令，恐涉改道之嫌。」

translations.literal: Now not following the book's command—I fear involving suspicion of changing the way.'
translations.idiomatic: Not to follow the book's command now may invite suspicion of changing her way.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「王孫、士安皆誨子以儉，送終之事，及其遵也，豈異今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Wang Sun and Shi'an both instructed sons in frugality; matters of seeing off the end—when sons followed, how does it differ from today?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: 'Wang Sun and Shi'an both instructed their sons in frugality in funeral matters; when sons followed, how does that differ from today?

sentences.zh: 改父之道者，蓋謂慢孝忘禮，肆情違度。

translations.literal: Changing the father's way means broadly speaking neglecting filial piety and forgetting ritual, giving free rein to feeling and violating measure.
translations.idiomatic: To change a father's way means to neglect filial piety, forget ritual, give free rein to feeling, and violate proper measure.

sentences.zh: 今梓宮之儉，玄房之約，明器幃帳，一無所陳。

translations.literal: Now the spirit coffin's frugality, the dark chamber's restraint, bright vessels and curtain hangings—not one thing is displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the spirit coffin's frugality, the dark chamber's restraint, bright vessels and curtain hangings—not one is displayed.

sentences.zh: 如斯之事，卿等所悉。

translations.literal: Such matters as these—you all know them.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as these you all know.

sentences.zh: 衰服之告，乃至聖心卑己申下之意，寧可苟順沖約之旨，而頓絕創巨之痛。

translations.literal: The announcement on mourning garments even reaches to the sage heart's humbling self and extending below—how can one perfunctorily follow the mild restraint's intent and abruptly cut off the pain of a wound greater than one's body?
translations.idiomatic: The announcement on mourning garments goes even to her sage heart's intent to humble herself and extend grace below—how can one perfunctorily follow the intent of mild restraint and abruptly cut off the pain of a wound greater than one's body?

sentences.zh: 縱有所涉，甘受後代之譏，未忍今日之請。

translations.literal: Even if it involves something, I gladly accept later generations' ridicule—I cannot bear today's requests.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I thereby invite censure from later generations, I gladly accept it—I cannot bear today's requests.

sentences.zh: 又表稱春秋烝嘗，事難廢闕。

translations.literal: Moreover your memorial says spring and autumn offerings and seasonal sacrifices—the affair is hard to abandon or omit.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial also says that spring and autumn offerings and seasonal sacrifices are hard to omit.

sentences.zh: 朕聞諸夫子，『吾不與祭，如不祭』。

translations.literal: I heard from the Master: 'If I do not participate in sacrifice, it is as if there were no sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: I heard from the Master, 'If I do not participate in sacrifice, it is as if there were no sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 自先朝以來，有司行事，不必躬親，比之聖言，於事殆闕。

translations.literal: Since former dynasties officials have conducted affairs—not necessarily in person. Compared to the sage's words, in the affair it is almost a lack.
translations.idiomatic: Since former dynasties officials have conducted the rites without the ruler necessarily attending in person; compared with the sage's words, the practice falls short.

sentences.zh: 賴蒙慈訓之恩，自行致敬之禮。

translations.literal: Relying on received kind instruction's grace, I myself carry out the rite of paying respect.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on the grace of her kind instruction, I myself shall perform the rites of reverence.

sentences.zh: 今昊天降罰，殃禍上延，人神喪恃，幽顯同切，想宗廟之靈，亦輟歆祀。

translations.literal: Now august Heaven sends down punishment; calamity and disaster extend upward; humans and spirits lose their reliance; hidden and manifest share the same keen grief—I think the ancestral temple spirits also cease their pleased sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has now sent down punishment; calamity reaches even above. Humans and spirits alike have lost their support; the living and the dead share the same anguish. I believe the spirits in the ancestral temples have also ceased to accept our offerings.

sentences.zh: 脫行饗薦，恐乖冥旨。

translations.literal: If I presumptuously carry out feasting and offerings, I fear it violates the obscure intent.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to proceed with feasting and offerings, I fear it would violate her intent in the unseen realm.

sentences.zh: 仰思成訓，倍增痛絕。

translations.literal: Looking up and reflecting on her accomplished instruction, grief doubles to the point of breaking.
translations.idiomatic: When I reflect on her accomplished instruction, my grief doubles unbearably.

sentences.zh: 豈忍身襲衮冕，親行吉事。」

translations.literal: How could I bear personally to don the dragon robe and crown and personally perform auspicious affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I bear to clothe myself in the dragon robe and crown and personally perform auspicious rites?"

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「古者郊天，越紼行事，宗廟之重，次於郊祀。

translations.literal: Gao Lü replied: "In antiquity when sacrificing to Heaven, one crossed the mourning sash to perform the rite; the weight of the ancestral temples was second only to the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lü replied, "In antiquity, when sacrificing to Heaven, one tied the mourning sash aside to perform the rite. The ancestral temples ranked second only to the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今山陵已畢，不可久廢廟饗。」

translations.literal: Now the mountain tomb is completed—it cannot be long that temple feasting is abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb rites are now complete; temple offerings cannot be suspended much longer."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「祭祀之典，事由聖經，未忍之心，具如前告。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "The canon of sacrifice derives from the sage classics; my heart's inability to bear it has been fully set forth as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "The canon of sacrifice derives from the sage classics. My heart's inability to bear it has been fully explained already.

sentences.zh: 脫至廟庭，號慕自纏，終恐廢禮。

translations.literal: If I were to reach the temple courtyard, my wailing grief would entangle itself—I ultimately fear the rite would be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to enter the temple courtyard, my wailing grief would overwhelm me, and I fear the rite would ultimately be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 公卿如能獨行，事在言外。」

translations.literal: If you ministers can perform it alone, the matter lies outside my words."
translations.idiomatic: If you ministers can perform the rites yourselves, that lies beyond what I can say."

sentences.zh: 李彪曰：「三年不為禮，禮必壞；

translations.literal: Li Biao said: "Three years without ritual—the ritual must decay;
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao said, "If for three years one does not practice ritual, ritual must decay;

sentences.zh: 三年不為樂，樂必崩。
