translations.literal: three years without music—music must collapse.
translations.idiomatic: if for three years one does not practice music, music must collapse.

sentences.zh: 今欲廢禮闕樂，臣等未敢。」

translations.literal: Now you wish to abandon ritual and omit music—we your ministers dare not."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty wishes to abandon ritual and omit music—we your ministers dare not consent."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此乃宰予不仁之說，己受責於孔子，不足復言。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "This is the inhumane doctrine of Zai Yu; he already received rebuke from Confucius—it is not worth speaking of again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "That is the inhumane doctrine of Zai Yu. He already received Confucius's rebuke and is not worth discussing again.

sentences.zh: 羣官前表，稱『高宗徒有諒闇之言，而無可遵之式』。

translations.literal: The officials' earlier memorial said 'Gaozong merely had words of mourning seclusion but no pattern to follow.'
translations.idiomatic: Your earlier memorial said, 'Gaozong merely spoke of mourning seclusion but left no pattern to follow.'

sentences.zh: 朕惟信闇默之難，周公禮制，自茲以降，莫能景行。

translations.literal: I trust that silent seclusion is difficult; Duke of Zhou's ritual system—from then down—none could model their conduct on it.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that silent seclusion is difficult to sustain. Since Duke of Zhou's ritual system, none has been able to model their conduct on it.

sentences.zh: 言無可遵之式，良可怪矣。

translations.literal: To say there is no pattern to follow is truly strange.
translations.idiomatic: To say there is no pattern to follow is truly strange.

sentences.zh: 復云，康王既廢初喪之儀，先行即位之禮。

translations.literal: It also said King Kang, having abandoned the initial mourning rites, first performed the rite of accession.
translations.idiomatic: It also said that King Kang, having set aside the initial mourning rites, first performed the accession ceremony.

sentences.zh: 於是無改之道式虧，三年之喪有缺。

translations.literal: Thus the undiminished way's pattern was impaired and the three-year mourning had a gap.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the pattern of the undiminished way was impaired, and the three-year mourning was left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 朕謂服美不安，先賢有諭；

translations.literal: I hold that to find fine garments uncomfortable—the former sages had instruction on this;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that finding fine garments uncomfortable—the former sages had instruction on this;

sentences.zh: 禮畢居喪，著在前典。

translations.literal: to complete the rites then dwell in mourning is recorded in former canons.
translations.idiomatic: and that one completes the rites and then dwells in mourning is recorded in the former canons.

sentences.zh: 或虧之言，有缺之義，深乖理衷。」

translations.literal: Words of impairment and meanings of gaps deeply violate what reason embraces."
translations.idiomatic: Words of impairment and meanings of incompleteness deeply violate what reason embraces."

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「臣等據案成事，依附杜預，多有未允。

translations.literal: Gao Lü replied: "We your ministers, relying on cases to complete the affair and attaching ourselves to Du Yu—much was not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lü replied, "We your ministers, relying on precedent to settle the matter and following Du Yu, found much that was not acceptable.

sentences.zh: 至乃推校古今，量考眾議，實如明旨。

translations.literal: Going so far as to compare ancient and modern and weigh all opinions—it truly accords with your enlightened intent.
translations.idiomatic: When we compared ancient and modern practice and weighed all opinions, we found it truly accords with Your Majesty's enlightened intent.

sentences.zh: 臣等竊惟曾參匹夫，七日不食，夫子以為非禮。

translations.literal: We privately consider: Zeng Shen was a common man; seven days without food—the Master deemed it contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: We privately reflect that Zeng Shen was but a common man. When he went seven days without food, the Master deemed it contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 及錄其事，唯書七日，不稱三年，蓋重其初慕之心。

translations.literal: When recording the affair, they only wrote seven days, not calling it three years—probably honoring his initial yearning heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was recorded, only seven days were written, not three years—probably because they honored the depth of his initial grief.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以萬乘之尊，不食竟於五日，既御則三食不充半溢。

translations.literal: We consider Your Majesty with the eminence of ten thousand chariots—not eating for five full days; once you resumed rule, three meals did not fill half a bowl.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, abstained from food for five full days, and that since resuming rule your three daily meals have not filled half a bowl.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏用悲惶，肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: We prostrate in grief and panic—our livers and brains smeared on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: We prostrate ourselves in grief and dread, ready to lay down our lives.

sentences.zh: 躬行一日，足以貫被幽顯，豈宜衰服三年，以曠機務。

translations.literal: Personally practicing for one day suffices to penetrate hidden and manifest—how should one wear mourning three years and neglect state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: A single day of personal observance suffices to reach both the living and the dead. How could one wear mourning for three years and neglect the affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 夫聖人制禮，不及者企而及之，過之者俯而就之。

translations.literal: The sage fashioned ritual: those who fall short strive to reach it; those who exceed bow and comply.
translations.idiomatic: The sage fashioned ritual so that those who fall short may strive to reach it and those who exceed may bow and comply.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下抑至慕之情，俯就典禮之重，誠是臣等慺慺之願。」

translations.literal: We pray Your Majesty will suppress utmost yearning feeling and bow to ritual canon's weight—truly our ministers' earnest wish."
translations.idiomatic: We pray that Your Majesty will restrain your utmost grief and bow to the weight of canonical ritual. That is truly our ministers' earnest wish."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「恩隆德厚，則思戀自深，雖非至情，由所感發。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "When grace is lofty and virtue thick, longing naturally runs deep; though not the utmost feeling, it arises from what one senses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "When grace is lofty and virtue profound, longing runs deep of itself. Though not the utmost feeling, it arises from what one has received.

sentences.zh: 然曾參之孝，曠代而有，豈朕今日所足論也。

translations.literal: Yet Zeng Shen's filial piety—rare across ages—how is it what I today am fit to discuss?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zeng Shen's filial piety appears only once in an age. How am I fit to be compared with him today?

sentences.zh: 又前表，稱『古者葬而即吉，不必終禮，此乃二漢所以經綸治道，魏晉所以綱理庶政』。

translations.literal: Again your earlier memorial said 'In antiquity burial then immediately auspicious dress—not necessarily completing the ritual—this is how the two Hans wove governance and how Wei and Jin regulated public affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Your earlier memorial also said, 'In antiquity one buried the dead and then immediately resumed auspicious dress without necessarily completing the full ritual. This is how the two Han dynasties wove their governance and how Wei and Jin regulated public affairs.'

sentences.zh: 朕以為既葬即吉，蓋其季俗多亂，權宜救世耳，諒非光治興邦之化。

translations.literal: I hold that burial-then-immediately-auspicious was probably because their decadent age's customs were chaotic—expedient to save the age—not surely the transformation that illumines governance and raises the state.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that resuming auspicious dress immediately after burial was probably because those decadent ages were chaotic and needed an expedient to save the realm—not the transformation that illumines governance and raises a state.

sentences.zh: 二漢之盛，魏晉之興，豈由簡略喪禮，遺忘仁孝哉。

translations.literal: Were the two Hans' flourishing and Wei and Jin's rise owing to simplifying mourning ritual and forgetting humaneness and filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: Did the flourishing of the two Han dynasties and the rise of Wei and Jin come from simplifying mourning ritual and forgetting humaneness and filial piety?

sentences.zh: 公卿偏執一隅，便謂經治之要，皆在於斯，殆非義也。

translations.literal: You ministers, clinging stubbornly to one corner, then say the essentials of governing all lie in this—hardly righteous.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers cling stubbornly to one point and then declare that the essentials of governing the realm all lie in this. That can hardly be called righteous.

sentences.zh: 昔平日之時，公卿每奏稱當今四海晏安，諸夏清泰，禮樂日新，政和民悅。

translations.literal: In former peaceful times you ministers each memorialized that the present age—within the four seas all is calm, all Xia are clear and peaceful, ritual and music daily renew, governance harmonious and people pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In former peaceful times you ministers repeatedly memorialized that the realm was tranquil within the four seas, that all the Xia lands were clear and peaceful, that ritual and music were daily renewed, and that governance was harmonious and the people content.

sentences.zh: 蹤侔軒唐，事等虞禹，漢魏已下，固不足仰止聖治。

translations.literal: Tracks matching Xuanyuan and Tang, affairs equal to Yu and Shun—Han and Wei downward certainly not worth looking up to stop at sage governance.
translations.idiomatic: Our tracks matched those of Xuanyuan and Tang; our affairs equaled those of Yu and Shun. Han and Wei and all below were certainly not worth looking up to as models of sage governance.

sentences.zh: 及至今日，便欲苦奪朕志，使不踰於魏晉。

translations.literal: Yet reaching today, you then wish bitterly to seize my intent and make me not exceed Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you wish bitterly to wrest away my intent and make me not exceed Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 如此之意，未解所由。

translations.literal: Such intent—I do not understand whence it comes.
translations.idiomatic: I do not understand whence such intent comes.

sentences.zh: 昔文母上承聖主之資，下有賢子之化，唯助德宣政，因風致穆而已。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Wen received above a sage lord's endowment, below had worthy son's transformation—only assisting virtue and spreading governance, riding the wind to bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Empress Wen received above the endowment of a sage sovereign and below the transformation of a worthy son. She only assisted virtue and spread governance, riding the wind to bring peace.

sentences.zh: 當今眾事草創，萬務惟始，朕以不德，沖年踐祚。

translations.literal: Today myriad affairs are newly founded, ten thousand tasks just beginning—I, lacking virtue, in tender years ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Today myriad affairs are newly founded and ten thousand tasks are just beginning. I, lacking in virtue, ascended the throne in my tender years.

sentences.zh: 而聖母匡訓以義方，詔誨以政事，經綸內外，憂勤億兆，使君臣協和，天下緝穆。

translations.literal: Yet the sage mother rectified instruction with the righteous method, edified with political affairs, wove inside and outside, worried and toiled for hundreds of millions, making lord and minister harmonious and all under Heaven tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage mother corrected my instruction with righteous principle, edified me in affairs of state, wove governance inside and out, and toiled in care for the hundred million people, so that lord and minister were harmonious and all under Heaven was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 上代已來，何后之功，得以仰比？

translations.literal: Since upper generations, what empress's achievement could be looked up to for comparison?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, what empress's achievement could be looked up to for comparison?

sentences.zh: 如有可擬，則從眾議。

translations.literal: If there is one to match, then follow the multitude's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: If there is one to match her, then I shall follow your counsel.

sentences.zh: 堯雖棄子禪舜，而舜自有聖德，不假堯成。

translations.literal: Though Yao abandoned his son and ceded to Shun, Shun himself had sage virtue—did not borrow Yao's completion.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yao set aside his son and ceded the throne to Shun, Shun possessed sage virtue of his own and did not owe his completion to Yao.

sentences.zh: 及其徂也，猶四海遏密，終於三年。

translations.literal: When he passed, still the four seas muffled music, ending only after three years.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed away, the four seas still muffled their music, and mourning did not end until three years had passed.

sentences.zh: 今慈育之恩，詔教之德，尋之曠代，未有匹擬。

translations.literal: Today fostering grace and edifying virtue—searching across distant ages, none to match.
translations.idiomatic: The grace of her fostering care and the virtue of her edifying instruction—searching across distant ages, there is none to match.

sentences.zh: 既受非常之恩，寧忍從其常式。

translations.literal: Having received extraordinary grace, how could I bear to follow ordinary pattern?
translations.idiomatic: Having received such extraordinary grace, how could I bear to follow the ordinary pattern?

sentences.zh: 況未殊一時，而公卿欲令即吉。

translations.literal: Moreover not yet a full season apart, yet you ministers wish to make me immediately auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, not even a full season has passed, yet you ministers wish to make me resume auspicious dress immediately.

sentences.zh: 冠冕黼黻，行禮廟庭；

translations.literal: Dragon robes and embroidered regalia, performing rites in the temple court;
translations.idiomatic: To don the crown and dragon robes and perform rites in the temple court;

sentences.zh: 臨軒設懸，饗會萬國。

translations.literal: facing the hall setting suspended music, feasting assembling ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: to face the hall with suspended music set up and feast with the myriad states—

sentences.zh: 尋事求心，實所未忍。」

translations.literal: weighing the affair against the heart—truly what I cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: when I weigh the affair against my heart, it is truly what I cannot bear."

sentences.zh: 高閭對曰：「臣等遵承冊令，因循前典，惟願除衰即吉，親理萬機。

translations.literal: Gao Lü replied: "We your ministers obey and receive the edict commands, follow former canon—we only wish to remove mourning and immediately be auspicious, personally administer the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lü replied, "We your ministers obey the edict commands and follow former canon. We only wish that Your Majesty remove mourning garments and resume auspicious dress immediately and personally administer the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 至德所在，陛下欽明稽古，周覽墳籍，孝性發於聖質，至情出於自然，斟酌古今，事非臣等所及。」

translations.literal: Where utmost virtue resides—Your Majesty respectfully bright, examining antiquity, comprehensively viewing tomb records—filial nature arising from sage substance, utmost feeling from the natural; weighing ancient and modern—affairs not what we ministers can reach."
translations.idiomatic: Where utmost virtue resides, Your Majesty is respectfully bright, examines antiquity, and has comprehensively reviewed the tomb classics. Filial nature arises from your sage substance and utmost feeling from the natural. In weighing ancient and modern practice, the affair is beyond what we your ministers can reach."

sentences.zh: 李彪曰：「當今雖治風緝穆，民庶晏然。

translations.literal: Li Biao said: "Though today governance's wind is tranquil and the people are at peace,
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao said, "Though today the winds of governance are tranquil and the people are at peace,

sentences.zh: 江南有未賓之吳，朔北有不臣之虜，東西二蕃雖文表稱順，情尚難測。

translations.literal: south of the Yangtze there is unsubmissive Wu, north of the frontier unsubmissive barbarians; east and west frontier domains though on paper claim obedience, sentiments are still hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: south of the Yangtze there is Wu, not yet submissive; north of the frontier there are barbarians who do not acknowledge our rule. The eastern and western frontier domains, though their documents claim obedience, remain hard to read in sentiment.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等猶懷不虞之慮。」

translations.literal: Therefore we your ministers still harbor unanticipated concerns."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we your ministers still harbor unanticipated concerns."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「魯公帶絰從師，晉侯墨衰敗寇，往聖無譏，前典所許。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "The Duke of Lu wore the mourning sash following his teacher; the Marquis of Jin in ink-dyed mourning defeated invaders—former sages did not criticize, former canon permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "The Duke of Lu wore the mourning sash while following his teacher; the Marquis of Jin, in ink-dyed mourning, defeated invaders. Former sages did not criticize this, and former canon permitted it.

sentences.zh: 如有不虞，雖越紼無嫌，而況衰麻乎？

translations.literal: If there is the unanticipated, though crossing the mourning sash without blame—how much more coarse hemp mourning?
translations.idiomatic: If the unexpected should arise, even crossing the mourning sash would be without blame—how much more so wearing coarse hemp mourning?

sentences.zh: 豈可於晏安之辰，豫念戎旅之事，以廢喪紀哉！」

translations.literal: How could one at a time of peaceful calm premeditate military affairs and thereby abandon mourning observance!"
translations.idiomatic: How could one, in a time of peaceful calm, premeditate military affairs and thereby abandon mourning observance!"

sentences.zh: 李彪對曰：「昔太伯父死適越，不失至德之名。

translations.literal: Li Biao replied: "Formerly Taibo's elder brother died while he was in Yue—he did not lose the name of utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao replied, "Formerly, when Taibo's elder brother died, Taibo was in Yue, yet he did not lose the name of utmost virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不懷，有由然也。

translations.literal: He surely yearned—there was reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Surely he yearned in his heart, yet there was reason for it.

sentences.zh: 伏願抑至慕之心，從遺告之重。

translations.literal: We pray you suppress utmost yearning and follow the weight of her testament.
translations.idiomatic: We pray that Your Majesty restrain your utmost grief and follow the weight of her testament.

sentences.zh: 臣聞知子莫若父母，聖后知陛下至孝之性也難奪，故豫造金冊，明著遺禮。

translations.literal: I hear: none knows a son like parents—the sage empress knew Your Majesty's utmost filial nature was hard to wrest away, therefore pre-made the golden edict, clearly setting forth the departing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that none knows a son like his parents. The sage empress knew that Your Majesty's utmost filial nature was hard to wrest away, and therefore pre-made the golden edict, clearly setting forth her departing ritual instructions.

sentences.zh: 今陛下孝慕深遠，果不可奪，臣等常辭，知何所啟。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's filial yearning is deep and far—it truly cannot be wrested away; we your ministers have spoken repeatedly—know not what to present."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's filial grief is deep and far-reaching and truly cannot be wrested away. We your ministers have spoken repeatedly and know not what further to present."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「太伯之言，有乖今事，諸情備如前論，更不重敍古義。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Taibo's words stray from today's affair; all circumstances are complete as argued before—I will not again recount ancient meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "Taibo's words do not fit today's affair. All the circumstances have been fully argued as before. I will not recount ancient meanings again.

sentences.zh: 亦有稱王者除衰而諒闇終喪者，若不許朕衰，朕則當除衰闇默，委政冢宰。

translations.literal: There are also those who say a king removes mourning but in silent seclusion completes mourning—if you do not permit me mourning, I shall remove mourning and in silent seclusion, entrust governance to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: There are also those who say that a king may remove mourning garments yet complete the mourning in silent seclusion. If you do not permit me to wear mourning, I shall remove mourning and dwell in silent seclusion, entrusting governance to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二事之中，惟公卿所擇。」

translations.literal: Between the two affairs—only for you ministers to choose."
translations.idiomatic: Between these two courses, let you ministers choose."

sentences.zh: 明根對曰：「陛下孝侔高宗，慕同大舜，服衰麻以申至痛，理萬機以從遺旨，興曠世之廢禮，制一代之高則。

translations.literal: Ming Gen replied: "Your Majesty's filial piety matches Gaozong, yearning equals Great Shun—wearing hemp mourning to express utmost pain, administering myriad affairs to follow the testament intent, raising long-abandoned ritual, establishing a generation's lofty norm.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Gen replied, "Your Majesty's filial piety matches Gaozong of Shang; your yearning equals that of Great Shun. You wear hemp mourning to express your utmost grief and administer the myriad affairs of state to follow her testament. You revive long-abandoned ritual and establish a lofty norm for the age.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏尋淵默不言，則代政將曠，仰順聖慕之心，請從衰服之旨。」

translations.literal: We prostrate and seek: deep silence without speech—then the generation's governance will be vacant; looking up to follow the sage yearning heart—we request to follow the intent of mourning garments."
translations.idiomatic: We reflect that if you dwell in deep silence and do not speak, governance for the age will lie vacant. Looking up to follow your sage grief, we request that you follow the intent of wearing mourning garments."

sentences.zh: 東陽王丕曰：「臣與尉元，歷事五帝，雖衰老無識，敢奏所聞。

translations.literal: Prince Pi of Dongyang said: "I and Yu Yuan served five emperors; though old and without understanding, we dare report what we heard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pi of Dongyang said, "Yu Yuan and I have served five emperors. Though old and without understanding, we dare report what we have heard.

sentences.zh: 自聖世以來，大諱之後三月，必須迎神於西，攘惡於北，具行吉禮。

translations.literal: Since the sage reigns, after the great taboo in the third month one must welcome spirits in the west, expel ill omens in the north, fully perform auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sage reigns began, in the third month after the great taboo one must welcome the spirits in the west, expel ill omens in the north, and fully perform the auspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 自皇始以來，未之或易。」

translations.literal: Since Huangshi—never changed."
translations.idiomatic: Since the Huangshi reign, this has never been altered."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「太尉國老，言先朝舊事，誠如所陳。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "The Grand Mentor, elder of the state—speaking of former court old affairs—it is truly as stated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "The Grand Mentor, elder of the state, speaks of former court affairs as they truly were.

sentences.zh: 但聰明正直，唯德是依。

translations.literal: But the intelligent and upright follow only virtue.
translations.idiomatic: But the intelligent and upright follow only virtue.

sentences.zh: 若能以道，不召自至。

translations.literal: If one can through the Way, without summoning they come of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If one can act through the Way, spirits come without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 苟失仁義，雖請弗來。

translations.literal: If one lacks humaneness and righteousness, though invited they will not come.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks humaneness and righteousness, though invited they will not come.

sentences.zh: 大禍三月，而備行吉禮，深在難忍。

translations.literal: Great calamity in the third month yet fully performing auspicious rites—deeply hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month after great calamity to fully perform auspicious rites is deeply hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 縱即吉之後，猶所不行，況數旬之中，而有此理。

translations.literal: Even after immediately auspicious—it still would not be done—how much more within several tens of days to have this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Even after resuming auspicious dress it would still be unthinkable—how much more so within a few tens of days.

sentences.zh: 恐是先朝萬得之一失，未可以為常式。

translations.literal: I fear it was the former court's one lapse in ten thousand—it cannot be made the regular pattern.
translations.idiomatic: I fear it was the former court's one lapse in ten thousand and cannot be made the regular pattern.

sentences.zh: 朕在不言之地，不應如此。

translations.literal: I am in the place of not speaking—I ought not be thus.
translations.idiomatic: I am in the place of not speaking and ought not be treated thus.

sentences.zh: 但公卿執奪，朕情未忍從，遂成往復，追用悲絕。」

translations.literal: But you ministers cling and seize; my feeling cannot bear to follow—thus it became back and forth, recalling this causes grief to break."
translations.idiomatic: But you ministers cling and press; my heart cannot bear to comply. Thus the exchange went back and forth, and to recall it renews my grief to the breaking point."

sentences.zh: 上遂號慟，羣官亦哭而辭出。

translations.literal: The Emperor then wailed loudly; the officials also wept and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then wailed aloud. The officials also wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬午詔曰：「公卿屢上啟事，依據金冊遺旨，中代成式，求過葬即吉。

translations.literal: On renwu day an edict said: "You ministers repeatedly submitted matters, relying on the golden edict's testament, middle-generation established pattern, seeking to pass burial then immediately auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu an edict said, "You ministers have repeatedly submitted memorials, relying on the golden edict's testament and the established pattern of middle antiquity, seeking to pass beyond burial and resume auspicious dress immediately.

sentences.zh: 朕仰惟恩重，不勝罔極之痛。

translations.literal: I look up considering grace's weight—cannot overcome boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: I look up and consider the weight of her grace and cannot overcome my boundless grief.

sentences.zh: 思遵遠古，終三年之禮。

translations.literal: Thinking to follow remote antiquity—the full three-year ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I had thought to follow remote antiquity and complete the full three-year ritual.

sentences.zh: 比見羣官具論所懷，今依禮既虞卒哭，剋此月二十日受服，以葛易麻。

translations.literal: Recently seeing officials fully state their thoughts—now according to ritual, having passed yu and zu ku, on the twentieth of this month I receive garments, replacing hemp with ge.
translations.idiomatic: Having recently seen the officials fully state their thoughts, I now follow ritual. Having passed the yu and zu ku observances, on the twentieth of this month I shall receive the changed garments, replacing hemp with ge cloth.

sentences.zh: 既衰服在上，公卿不得獨釋於下。

translations.literal: Since mourning garments are on high, officials cannot alone release below.
translations.idiomatic: Since mourning garments are worn above, officials below cannot release theirs alone.

sentences.zh: 故於朕之授變從練，已下復為節降。

translations.literal: Therefore from my granting the change to follow dian, below again made graduated reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, from my granting the change to follow the dian mourning stage downward, graduated reductions are again made.

sentences.zh: 斷度今古，以情制衷。

translations.literal: Judging ancient and modern, using feeling to regulate the center.
translations.idiomatic: I have judged ancient and modern practice and regulated the mean according to feeling.

sentences.zh: 但取遺旨速除之一節，粗申臣子哀慕之深情。

translations.literal: Only taking the testament's one section on swift removal—to roughly express ministers and subjects' deep mourning yearning.
translations.idiomatic: I take only the one section of her testament on swift removal, to give rough expression to the deep mourning yearning of ministers and subjects.

sentences.zh: 欲令百官同知此意，故用宣示。

translations.literal: Wishing to make all officials know this intent—therefore use proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: I wish all officials to know this intent and therefore proclaim it.

sentences.zh: 便及變禮，感痛彌深。」

translations.literal: Now reaching the change ritual—felt pain grows deeper."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the change in ritual is upon us, my grief grows deeper still."

sentences.zh: 十五年四月癸亥朔，設薦於太和廟。

translations.literal: Year 15, 4th month, guihai first day—establish offerings at Taihe Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, on the first day of the fourth month, the day guihai, offerings were established at the Taihe Temple.

sentences.zh: 是日，高祖及從服者仍朝夕臨，始進蔬食，上哀哭追感不飯。

translations.literal: That day, Gaozu and those following mourning garments still attended morning and evening; first introduced vegetable food; the Emperor mourning and weeping, recalling grief, would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: That day Emperor Gaozu and those in mourning garments still attended morning and evening. Vegetable food was first introduced. The Emperor, mourning and weeping in recollection of grief, would not eat.

sentences.zh: 侍中、南平王馮誕等諫，經宿乃膳。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief, Prince Dan of Nanping Feng Dan and others remonstrated—after a night he then took food.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-chief, Prince Dan of Nanping Feng Dan, and others remonstrated with him. After a full night he finally took food.

sentences.zh: 甲子罷朝，夕哭。

translations.literal: On jiazi day court was dismissed; evening weeping.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi court was dismissed and evening mourning was observed.

sentences.zh: 九月丙戌，有司上言求卜祥日。

translations.literal: 9th month bingxu— the relevant offices submitted seeking to divine the auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day bingxu, the relevant offices submitted a memorial requesting divination of an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「便及此期，覽以摧絕。

translations.literal: Edict said: "Now reaching this date—reading it my spirit is shattered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Now that this date is upon us, to read the memorial shatters my spirit.

sentences.zh: 敬祭卜祥，乃古之成典。

translations.literal: Reverent offerings and divination for auspiciousness are indeed an ancient established canon.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent sacrifice and divination for an auspicious day are an established canon of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 但世失其義，筮日求吉，[2]既乖敬事之志，又違永慕之心。

translations.literal: But the age has lost their meaning—divining days to seek fortune [2] both departs from the intent of reverent service and violates the heart of everlasting longing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age has lost their meaning: to divine a day and seek good fortune [2] both betrays the spirit of reverent observance and runs counter to the heart's everlasting grief.

sentences.zh: 今將屈禮厲眾，不訪龜兆。

translations.literal: Now I shall bend ritual to exhort the multitude and not consult turtle omens.
translations.idiomatic: Now I shall bend ritual to steel the multitude and will not consult turtle omens.

sentences.zh: 已企及此晦，寧敢重違冊旨，以異羣議。

translations.literal: Already I have looked to this month's end—how dare I again violate the edict's intent and differ from the assembly's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I have already set my hopes on this month's end; how could I again defy the edict's intent and stand apart from the assembly's counsel?

sentences.zh: 尋惟永往，言增崩裂。」

translations.literal: Reflecting on everlasting departure, words only add to collapse and rending."
translations.idiomatic: When I reflect on her everlasting departure, every word only deepens my collapse and grief."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，高祖宿於廟。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Gaozu lodged at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Emperor Gaozu lodged overnight at the temple.

sentences.zh: 至夜一刻，引諸王、三都大官、駙馬、三公、令僕已下，奏事中散已上，及刺史、鎮將，立哭於廟庭，三公、令僕升廟。

translations.literal: Reaching the first quarter of the night, he led the princes, grand officials of the three capitals, imperial sons-in-law, the Three Excellencies, directors and vice directors downward, memorialists and palace attendant draftsmen upward, and regional inspectors and garrison commanders to stand weeping in the temple courtyard; the Three Excellencies and directors and vice directors ascended the temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the first quarter of the night, he summoned the princes, grand officials of the three capitals, imperial sons-in-law, the Three Excellencies, and all officials from directors and vice directors on down, together with memorialists and palace attendant draftsmen on up, as well as regional inspectors and garrison commanders, to stand weeping in the temple courtyard; the Three Excellencies and the directors and vice directors ascended into the temple.

sentences.zh: 既出，監御令陳服笥於廟陛南，近侍者奉而升列於堊室前席。

translations.literal: After they came out, the Supervisor of Imperial Wardrobe displayed the garment chest at the south of the temple steps; attendants bore it up and arranged it before the seats in front of the whitewashed chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When they came out, the Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe set out the garment chest at the south side of the temple steps; attendants carried it up and laid out the garments before the seats in front of the whitewashed mourning chamber.

sentences.zh: 侍中、南平王馮誕跽奏請易服，進縞冠、皂朝服、革帶、黑屨，侍臣各易以黑介幘、白絹單衣、革帶、烏履，遂哀哭至乙夜，盡戊子。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief and Prince of Nanping Feng Dan knelt and submitted requesting change of garments, presenting unbleached hemp caps, black court robes, leather belts, and black shoes; attendant ministers each changed to black kerchiefs, white silk single garments, leather belts, and black shoes—then mourned and wept until the second watch of the night, through the day wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-chief, Prince Dan of Nanping Feng Dan, knelt and submitted a request to change garments, presenting unbleached hemp caps, black court robes, leather belts, and black shoes; the attendant ministers each changed into black kerchiefs, white silk single garments, leather belts, and black shoes, then mourned and wept until the second watch of the night and on through the day wuzi.

sentences.zh: 質明薦羞，奏事中散已上，冠服如侍臣，刺史已下無變。

translations.literal: At dawn delicacies were presented; memorialists and palace attendant draftsmen upward wore caps and garments like the attendant ministers; regional inspectors downward had no change.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, delicacies were presented as offerings; memorialists and palace attendant draftsmen on up wore caps and garments like the attendant ministers, while regional inspectors on down made no change of dress.

sentences.zh: 高祖薦酌，神部尚書王諶讚祝訖，哭拜遂出。

translations.literal: Gaozu presented libations; Director of the Ministry of Spirits Wang Chen intoned the invocation and finished, then weeping and bowing they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu presented the libations; Wang Chen, Director of the Ministry of Spirits, intoned the invocation to its end, and after weeping and bowing they departed.

sentences.zh: 有司陽祥服如前。

translations.literal: The relevant offices displayed auspicious garments as before.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices displayed the auspicious garments as before.

sentences.zh: [3]侍中跽奏，請易祭服，進縞冠素紕、白布深衣、麻繩履。

translations.literal: [3] The attendant-in-chief knelt and submitted, requesting change to sacrificial garments, presenting unbleached hemp caps with plain borders, white cloth deep garments, and hemp-rope shoes.
translations.idiomatic: [3] The attendant-in-chief knelt and submitted a request to change into sacrificial garments, presenting unbleached hemp caps with plain borders, white cloth deep garments, and hemp-rope shoes.

sentences.zh: 侍臣去幘易幍，羣官易服如侍臣，又引入如前。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers removed kerchiefs and changed to mourning caps; the host of officials changed garments like the attendant ministers, and were again led in as before.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant ministers removed their kerchiefs and changed into mourning caps; the host of officials changed garments like the attendant ministers and were again led in as before.

sentences.zh: 儀曹尚書游明根升廟跽慰，復位哭，遂出。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Rites You Minggen ascended the temple, knelt in consolation, returned to position and wept, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, Director of the Bureau of Rites, ascended the temple, knelt to offer consolation, returned to his place and wept, then departed.

sentences.zh: 引太守外臣及諸部渠帥入哭，次引蕭賾使并雜客入。

translations.literal: He led in grand administrators, outer subjects, and chieftains of the various tribes to weep; next led in the envoy of Xiao Ze and miscellaneous guests.
translations.idiomatic: He then led in grand administrators, outer subjects, and chieftains of the various tribes to weep; next he led in the envoy of Xiao Ze and miscellaneous guests.

sentences.zh: 至甲夜四刻，侍御、散騎常侍、司衞監以上升廟哭，既而出。

translations.literal: Reaching the fourth quarter of the first watch of the night, palace attendants, regular palace attendant cavalrymen, and supervisors of the palace guard upward ascended the temple to weep, then came out.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth quarter of the first watch of the night, palace attendants, regular palace attendant cavalrymen, and supervisors of the palace guard on up ascended the temple to weep, then came out.

sentences.zh: 帝出廟，停立哀哭，久而乃還。

translations.literal: The Emperor came out of the temple, halted and stood mourning and weeping, and only after a long while returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came out of the temple, halted and stood there mourning and weeping, and only after a long while returned.

sentences.zh: 十月，太尉丕奏曰：「竊聞太廟已就，明堂功畢，然享祀之禮，不可久曠。

translations.literal: 10th month—Grand Commandant Pi submitted: "I have heard in private that the Grand Temple is complete and the Bright Hall finished, yet the rites of sacrifice and offering cannot long be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Grand Commandant Pi submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the Grand Temple is complete and work on the Bright Hall finished, yet the rites of sacrifice and offering cannot long be neglected.

sentences.zh: 至於移廟之日，須得國之大姓，遷主安廟。

translations.literal: As for the day of transferring the temple, one must have the great clans of the state to move the spirit tablets and settle them in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the temple is transferred, the great clans of the state must be obtained to move the spirit tablets and install them in the temple.

sentences.zh: 神部尚書王諶既是庶姓，不宜參豫。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Spirits Wang Chen, being of a common clan, is not fit to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, Director of the Ministry of Spirits, is of a common clan and is not fit to take part.

sentences.zh: 臣昔以皇室宗屬，遷世祖之主。

translations.literal: Your subject formerly, as a member of the imperial house clan, moved the tablet of Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject formerly moved the tablet of Emperor Shizu in my capacity as a member of the imperial house clan.

sentences.zh: 先朝舊式，不敢不聞。」

translations.literal: The former court's old pattern—I dare not fail to report it."
translations.idiomatic: This was the former court's established practice, and I dare not fail to report it."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「具聞所奏，尋惟平日，倍增痛絕。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I have fully heard what was submitted; reflecting on ordinary days, grief is doubled and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "I have fully heard your memorial; when I reflect on ordinary days, my grief is doubled and cut off.

sentences.zh: 今遵述先旨，營建寢廟，既而粗就。

translations.literal: Now following and carrying out the former intent, the resting temple was built and is roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Now, following my predecessor's intent, the resting temple has been built and is roughly complete.

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，職司有分。

translations.literal: When the former kings established ritual, offices had their divisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the former kings established ritual, each office had its proper division of duty.

sentences.zh: 移廟之日，遷奉神主，皆太尉之事，朕亦親自行事，不得越局，專委大姓。

translations.literal: On the day of transferring the temple, moving and presenting the spirit tablets are all matters of the Grand Commandant; I too shall personally perform the rites and may not overstep office and exclusively entrust great clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the temple is transferred, moving and presenting the spirit tablets are all the Grand Commandant's affairs; I too shall personally perform the rites and may not overstep office to entrust this exclusively to great clans.

sentences.zh: 王諶所司，惟贊板而已。

translations.literal: What Wang Chen's office handles is only intoning the invocation board.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen's office is responsible only for intoning the invocation board.

sentences.zh: 時運流速，奄及縞制，復不得哀哭於明堂，後當親拜山陵，寫泄哀慕。」

translations.literal: Time's current flows swiftly; suddenly reaching unbleached hemp mourning, again I cannot mourn and weep in the Bright Hall; later I shall personally pay respects at the mountain tomb and pour out my grief and longing."
translations.idiomatic: Time flows swiftly; I have suddenly reached the period of unbleached hemp mourning and again cannot mourn and weep in the Bright Hall; later I shall personally pay my respects at the mountain tomb and pour out my grief and longing."

sentences.zh: 是年，高麗王死，十二月詔曰：「高麗王璉守蕃東隅，累朝貢職，年踰期頤，勤德彌著。

translations.literal: That year the King of Goguryeo died; in the 12th month an edict said: "King Rian of Goguryeo guarded the eastern frontier, through successive reigns performed tribute duties, his years passed the age of one hundred, and diligent virtue grew ever more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: That year the king of Goguryeo died. In the twelfth month an edict said, "King Rian of Goguryeo guarded the eastern frontier, through successive reigns fulfilled his tribute duties, lived beyond a hundred years, and his diligent virtue grew ever more manifest.

sentences.zh: 今既不幸，其赴使垂至，將為之舉哀。

translations.literal: Now that misfortune has come, his envoy of condolence is about to arrive; I shall hold mourning for him.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this misfortune has come, his envoy of condolence is about to arrive, and I shall hold mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 而古者同姓哭廟，異姓隨其方，皆有服制。

translations.literal: Yet in antiquity those of the same surname wept in the temple, those of different surnames followed their region—each had garment regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity those of the same surname wept in the temple, while those of different surnames followed the customs of their region; each had prescribed mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 今既久廢，不可卒為之衰，且欲素委貌、白布深衣，於城東為盡一哀，以見其使也。

translations.literal: Now that it has long been abandoned, one cannot suddenly make full mourning garments for him; for the time I wish plain caps and white cloth deep garments, and at the east of the city to exhaust one mourning observance, so as to receive his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: That practice has long been abandoned, and I cannot suddenly adopt full mourning for him; for now I wish to wear a plain cap and white cloth deep garments and, east of the city, perform a full mourning observance to receive his envoy.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不嘗識此人，甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Though I have never met this man, I deeply mourn and cherish him.
translations.idiomatic: Although I never met this man in person, I deeply mourn and cherish him.

sentences.zh: 有司可申敕備辦。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices may proclaim the order and prepare everything."
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices proclaim the order and make all preparations."

sentences.zh: 事如別儀。

translations.literal: The matter followed separate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was carried out according to separate regulations.

sentences.zh: 十六年九月辛未，高祖哭於文明太后陵左，終日不絕聲，幕越席為次，侍臣侍哭。

translations.literal: Year 16, 9th month xinwei—Gaozu wept at the left of Empress Dowager Wenming's tomb, all day without ceasing sound; curtains and rush mats were set as lodging; attendant ministers attended the weeping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on the day xinwei of the ninth month, Emperor Gaozu wept to the left of Empress Dowager Wenming's tomb, all day without ceasing; curtains and rush mats were set up as his lodging, and attendant ministers attended the mourning.

sentences.zh: 壬申，高祖以忌日哭於陵左，哀至則哭，侍哭如昨。

translations.literal: Renshen—Gaozu on the anniversary day wept at the left of the tomb; when grief came he wept; attendant weeping as yesterday.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, Emperor Gaozu wept at the left of the tomb on the anniversary of her death; whenever grief overcame him he wept, and the attendant ministers mourned as on the previous day.

sentences.zh: 帝二日不御膳。

translations.literal: The Emperor for two days did not take meals.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took no meals for two days.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，朝中夕三時，哭拜於陵前。

translations.literal: Guiyou—in court morning, midday, and evening three times, weeping and bowing before the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiyou, at morning, midday, and evening, he wept and bowed before the tomb.

sentences.zh: 夜宿監玄殿，是夜徹次。

translations.literal: At night he lodged in the Jianxuan Hall; that night the encampment was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: At night he lodged in the Jianxuan Hall; that night the mourning encampment was struck.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝拜哭辭陵，還永樂宮。

translations.literal: Jiaxu—the Emperor bowed, wept, and took leave of the tomb, returning to the Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, the Emperor bowed, wept, and took leave of the tomb, then returned to the Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太師馮熙薨，有數子尚幼。

translations.literal: Year 19—Grand Tutor Feng Xi died; he had several sons still young.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, leaving several sons still young.

sentences.zh: 議者以為童子之節，事降成人，謂為衰而不裳，免而不絰，又無腰麻繆垂，唯有絞帶。

translations.literal: Deliberators held that a child's observances, affairs being reduced from an adult's, meant wearing mourning garment without skirt, removing cap without hemp sash, and also having no waist hemp with dangling ends—only a twisted sash.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators held that a child's observances, being reduced from those of an adult, meant wearing the mourning garment without a skirt, removing the cap without a hemp sash, and having no waist hemp with dangling ends—only a twisted sash.

sentences.zh: 時博士孫惠蔚上書言：「臣雖識謝古人，然微涉傳記。

translations.literal: At the time Erudite Sun Huiwei submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, though my knowledge falls short of the ancients, yet has lightly touched upon transmitted records.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Erudite Sun Huiwei submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject, though my knowledge falls short of the ancients, has lightly studied transmitted records.

sentences.zh: 近取諸身，遠取諸禮，驗情以求理，尋理以推制。

translations.literal: Taking near from the person, taking far from ritual, testing feeling to seek principle, tracing principle to infer regulation.
translations.idiomatic: I take what is near from human experience and what is far from ritual, test feeling to seek principle, and trace principle to infer regulation.

sentences.zh: 竊謂童子在幼之儀，居喪之節，冠杖之制，有降成人。

translations.literal: I venture to hold that for a child, observances in youth, rules in dwelling in mourning, and regulations for cap and staff have reductions from an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to hold that for a child, observances in youth, rules for dwelling in mourning, and regulations for cap and staff are all reduced from those of an adult.

sentences.zh: 衰麻之服，略為不異。

translations.literal: Garments of coarse hemp mourning are broadly not different.
translations.idiomatic: The garments of coarse hemp mourning are broadly not different.

sentences.zh: 以玉藻二簡，微足明之，曰：童子之節，錦紳并紐。

translations.literal: From two passages of Jade Ornament, this is slightly sufficient to clarify it, saying: A child's observances—brocade sash and girdle-knot together.
translations.idiomatic: Two passages from Jade Ornament are enough to clarify this: it says, "A child's observances: brocade sash and girdle knot together."

sentences.zh: 錦紳即大帶，[4]既有佩觿之革，又有錦紐之紳。

translations.literal: Brocade sash is the great girdle; [4] there is both the leather for suspending the girdle pendant and also the brocade-knotted sash.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade sash is the great girdle; [4] there is both the leather strap for the girdle pendant and also the brocade-knotted sash.

sentences.zh: 此明童子雖幼，已備二帶。

translations.literal: This clarifies that though a child is young, he already has both girdles complete.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that though a child is young, he already wears both girdles.

sentences.zh: 以凶類吉，則腰絰存焉。

translations.literal: Applying the inauspicious category to the auspicious, then the waist hemp sash remains.
translations.idiomatic: When the inauspicious category is applied to the auspicious, the waist hemp sash remains.

sentences.zh: 又曰：童子無緦服。

translations.literal: It also says: A child has no fifth-degree mourning garment.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "A child wears no fifth-degree mourning garment."

sentences.zh: 鄭注曰：『雖不服緦，猶免深衣。』

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: "Though not wearing fifth-degree mourning, he still removes the deep garment."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary says, "Though he does not wear fifth-degree mourning, he still removes the deep garment."

sentences.zh: 是許其有裳，但不殊上下。

translations.literal: This permits him to have a skirt, but without distinguishing upper and lower.
translations.idiomatic: This permits him to wear a skirt, but without distinguishing upper and lower garments.

sentences.zh: 又深衣之制，長幼俱服。

translations.literal: Moreover the regulation of the deep garment—elder and younger alike wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the regulation of the deep garment is that elder and younger alike wear it.

sentences.zh: 童子為服之緦，猶免深衣，況居有服之斬，而反無裳乎？

translations.literal: For a child wearing fifth-degree mourning he still removes the deep garment—how much more when dwelling in the most severe mourning with garments, yet conversely having no skirt?
translations.idiomatic: When a child wears fifth-degree mourning he still removes the deep garment—how much more when he is in the most severe mourning, yet is said to have no skirt?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞先師舊說，童子常服類深衣，衰裳所施，理或取象。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard the old explanation of former masters: a child's ordinary garment resembles the deep garment; what is applied in mourning skirt may in principle take it as model.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard the old explanation of former masters: a child's ordinary garment resembles the deep garment, and what is applied in the mourning skirt may in principle take that as its model.

sentences.zh: 但典無成言，故未敢孤斷。

translations.literal: But the canon has no settled statement, so I have not dared to decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: But the canon has no settled statement on this, so I have not dared to decide alone.

sentences.zh: 又曰：聽事則不麻。

translations.literal: It also says: When attending to affairs, then no hemp.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "When attending to affairs, then no hemp."

sentences.zh: 則知不聽事麻矣。

translations.literal: Then one knows that when not attending to affairs there is hemp.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that when not attending to affairs, hemp is worn.

sentences.zh: 故注曰：『無麻往給事。』

translations.literal: Therefore the commentary says: "Without hemp when going to perform duties."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the commentary says, "Without hemp when going to perform duties."

sentences.zh: 此明族人之喪，童子有事，貫絰帶麻，執事不易，故暫聽去之，以便其使。

translations.literal: This clarifies that at a clansman's mourning, when a child has duties, he threads the sash and wears hemp; holding office is not easy to change, so for the time he is permitted to remove it, to facilitate his service.
translations.idiomatic: This clarifies that at a clansman's mourning, when a child has duties to perform, he threads the sash and wears hemp; because holding office makes it hard to change garments, he is temporarily permitted to remove them to facilitate his service.

sentences.zh: 往則不麻，不往則絰。

translations.literal: When going, then no hemp; when not going, then sash.
translations.idiomatic: When he goes, then no hemp; when he does not go, then the sash.

sentences.zh: 如使童子本自無麻，禮腰、首，聽與不聽，俱闕兩絰，唯舉無麻，足明不備，豈得言聽事則不麻乎？

translations.literal: If a child originally had no hemp by nature, then in ritual waist and head, whether attending or not attending, both would lack the two sashes—yet only "no hemp" is mentioned, sufficient to show incompleteness; how could one say "when attending to affairs, then no hemp"?
translations.idiomatic: If a child originally had no hemp at all, then for waist and head in ritual, whether attending to affairs or not, both sashes would be lacking—yet only "no hemp" is mentioned, which is enough to show the rule is incomplete; how then could one say "when attending to affairs, then no hemp"?

sentences.zh: 以此論之，有絰明矣。

translations.literal: Discussing it by this, having the sash is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this argument, the sash is clearly required.

sentences.zh: 且童子不杖不廬之節，理儉於責；

translations.literal: Moreover the observances of a child not carrying staff and not building hut—in principle they are sparing in what is required;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the observances by which a child does not carry a staff and does not build a mourning hut are, in principle, sparing in what is required;

sentences.zh: [5]不裳不絰之制，未覩其說。

translations.literal: [5] the regulation of no skirt and no sash—I have not seen its explanation.
translations.idiomatic: [5] as for the regulation of no skirt and no sash, I have never seen its explanation.

sentences.zh: 又臣竊解童子不衣裳之記，是有間之言。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject ventures to interpret the record that a child does not wear skirt and garment—it is a statement with qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I venture to interpret the record that a child does not wear skirt and garment as a qualified statement.

sentences.zh: [6]將謂童子時甫稚齡，未就外傅，出則不交族人，內則事殊長者，餕旨父母之前，往來慈乳之手，故許其無裳，以便易之。

translations.literal: [6] I would say that when a child is just in tender years, not yet gone to an outer tutor, going out he does not mingle with clansmen, within he serves differently from elders, receiving food before parents, coming and going in the hands of loving nurses—therefore he is permitted no skirt, to facilitate ease.
translations.idiomatic: [6] I would say that when a child is still in tender years, not yet sent to an outer tutor, he does not mingle with clansmen when he goes out and serves elders differently within the home, receiving food before his parents and passing constantly through the hands of loving nurses—therefore he is permitted to go without a skirt for ease.

sentences.zh: 若在志學之後，將冠之初，年居二九，質並成人，受道成均之學，釋菜上庠之內，將命孔氏之門，執燭曾參之室，而唯有掩身之衣，無蔽下之裳，臣愚未之安矣。

translations.literal: If after the age of aspiring to study, at the beginning of approaching capping, years reaching eighteen, substance equal to an adult, receiving the Way in the learning of the Imperial Academy, presenting vegetables within the upper school, about to be sent to Confucius's gate, holding candles in Zeng Shen's chamber—yet having only garments covering the body and no skirt covering below, your subject in folly is not at ease with this.
translations.idiomatic: But after the age of aspiring to study, at the threshold of capping, at eighteen with the substance of an adult, receiving instruction at the Imperial Academy, presenting vegetables in the upper school, about to be sent to Confucius's gate and hold candles in Zeng Shen's chamber—yet having only garments covering the body and no skirt below, I in my folly cannot be at ease with this.

sentences.zh: 又女子未許嫁，二十則笄，觀祭祀，納酒漿，助奠廟堂之中，視禮至敬之處，其於婉容之服，寧無其備。

translations.literal: Moreover a woman not yet betrothed, at twenty then capped with hairpin, observing sacrifices, presenting wine and gruel, assisting in offering within the temple hall, viewing ritual at the place of utmost reverence—for her graceful garments, would she not have their completeness?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a woman not yet betrothed is capped with a hairpin at twenty, observes sacrifices, presents wine and gruel, and assists at offerings within the temple hall at the place of utmost reverence—for her graceful garments, would she not have what is required?

sentences.zh: 以此推之，則男女雖幼，理應有裳。

translations.literal: Pushing this to infer, then though male and female are young, in principle they ought to have skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Inferring from this, though male and female are young, in principle they ought to wear skirts.

sentences.zh: 但男女未冠，禮謝三加，女子未出，衣殊狄褖。

translations.literal: But male and female not yet capped, ritual declines the three additions; a woman not yet married out, garments differ in Di-style padded robes.
translations.idiomatic: But when male and female are not yet capped, ritual declines the three additions; when a woman is not yet married out, her garments differ in Di-style padded robes.

sentences.zh: 無名之服，禮文罕見。

translations.literal: Garments without established names—ritual texts rarely show them.
translations.idiomatic: Garments without established names are rarely described in ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 童子雖不當室，苟以成人之心，則許其人服緦之絰。

translations.literal: Though a child does not head the household, if with an adult's heart, then he is permitted the person to wear the fifth-degree mourning sash.
translations.idiomatic: Though a child does not head the household, if he is treated with an adult's heart, he is permitted to wear the fifth-degree mourning sash.

sentences.zh: 輕猶有絰，斬重無麻，是為與輕而奪重，非禮之意，此臣之所以深疑也。

translations.literal: Light mourning still has sash; severe cutting mourning has no hemp—this is to give light and seize from heavy, not ritual's intent; this is why your subject deeply doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Light mourning still has a sash, yet the most severe mourning has no hemp—this would give light mourning what is denied to heavy mourning, contrary to ritual's intent; this is why I deeply doubt it.

sentences.zh: 又衰傍有袵，以掩裳際，如使無裳，袵便徒設，若復去袵，衰又不備。

translations.literal: Moreover beside the mourning garment is a lapel to cover the skirt's edge—if there were no skirt, the lapel would be set in vain; if again removing the lapel, the mourning garment would also be incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, beside the mourning garment is a lapel to cover the skirt's edge—if there were no skirt, the lapel would serve no purpose; if the lapel were removed as well, the mourning garment would be incomplete.

sentences.zh: 設有齊斬之故，而便成童男女唯服無袵之衰，去其裳絰，此必識禮之所不行，亦以明矣。

translations.literal: Suppose there were a reason for second- and third-degree mourning, yet then boys and girls in maturity wore only mourning garments without lapels, removing skirt and sash—this must be what those who know ritual will not practice; it is also clear.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose there were occasion for second- or third-degree mourning, yet boys and girls nearing maturity wore only mourning garments without lapels and removed skirt and sash—those who know ritual would never permit this; that too is clear.

sentences.zh: 若不行於己，而立制於人，是為違制以為法，從制以誤人。

translations.literal: If not practiced on oneself yet establishing regulation for others, this is to violate regulation and make it law, following regulation to mislead people.
translations.idiomatic: If one will not practice it oneself yet establishes a regulation for others, that is to violate regulation and make it law, and to follow regulation in order to mislead people.

sentences.zh: 恕禮而行，理將異此。」

translations.literal: Acting by excusing ritual—in principle it will differ from this."
translations.idiomatic: To act by setting ritual aside would, in principle, be quite different."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict followed his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 百禮咸畢 百衲本「百禮」二字空二格，南本已下諸本並注「闕二字」，今據通典卷八０總論喪期後魏條補。

translations.literal: All rites complete—In the patchwork edition the two characters "all rites" are blank for two spaces; the Southern edition and editions below all note "two characters missing"; now supplemented according to the Northern Wei entry on mourning periods in the general discussion of Book 80 of the Tongdian.
translations.idiomatic: All rites complete: In the patchwork edition the two characters bai li are left blank for two spaces; the Southern edition and later editions all note "two characters missing"; the text is now restored from the Northern Wei entry on mourning periods in the general discussion, juan 80 of the Tongdian.

sentences.zh: 筮日求吉 諸本作「筮曰永吉」，通鑑卷一三七

translations.literal: Divining day to seek fortune—all editions read "divining day eternal fortune"; Comprehensive Mirror juan 137
translations.idiomatic: Divining a day to seek good fortune: all editions read "divining a day for eternal good fortune"; Zizhi Tongjian, juan 137

sentences.zh: 〈四三一三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4313〉

sentences.zh: 如上摘句。

translations.literal: As the quoted passage above.
translations.idiomatic: As quoted above.

sentences.zh: 按上云「有司上言，求卜祥日」，知通鑑是，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining the text above, which says "the relevant offices submitted seeking to divine the auspicious day," one knows the Comprehensive Mirror is correct; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Since the passage above reads "the relevant offices submitted a memorial requesting divination of an auspicious day," the Zizhi Tongjian reading is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 有司陽祥服如前 按「陽」字不可解，上云「監御令陳服笥於廟陛南」，此云「如前」，疑「陽」乃「陳」之訛。

translations.literal: Relevant offices display auspicious garments as before—Examining: the character "display" is inexplicable; above it says "Supervisor of Imperial Wardrobe displayed garment chest at south of temple steps," here it says "as before"—suspected that "display" is corruption of "display/set out."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices displayed the auspicious garments as before: the character yang is inexplicable; the passage above says "the Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe set out the garment chest at the south of the temple steps," and here it says "as before"—yang is suspected to be a corruption of chen ("set out").

sentences.zh: 錦紳并紐錦紳即大帶 諸本「紐」作「細」，下「錦紳」無「紳」字。

translations.literal: Brocade sash and knot; brocade sash is great girdle—all editions read "knot" as "fine," and below "brocade sash" lacks the character "sash."
translations.idiomatic: Brocade sash and knot; brocade sash is the great girdle: all editions read niu as xi ("fine"), and below jin shen lacks the character shen.

sentences.zh: 冊府卷五八０

translations.literal: Ce fu juan 580
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Archives, juan 580

sentences.zh: 〈六九五六頁〉

sentences.zh: 如上摘句。

translations.literal: As the quoted passage above.
translations.idiomatic: As quoted above.

sentences.zh: 按禮記玉藻本文作紐，正義謂「絇，帶之紐」，「細」字無義，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining: Record of Rites Jade Ornament's main text reads "knot"; Correct Meaning says "knot of girdle"; the character "fine" has no meaning—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The main text of Record of Rites, "Jade Ornament," reads niu; the Correct Meaning gloss says "the knot of the girdle"; the character xi has no meaning here, and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又「錦紳」連文，「錦」不得云「即大帶」，今據補。

translations.literal: Moreover "brocade sash" is continuous text—"brocade" cannot be said to mean "that is, great girdle"; now supplemented accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, jin shen is a continuous phrase, so jin alone cannot mean "that is, the great girdle"; the text is supplemented accordingly.

sentences.zh: 且童子不杖不廬之節理儉於責 諸本「責」下旁注「疑」字。

translations.literal: Moreover a child's observances of not staff and not hut—in principle sparing in requirement—all editions have a side note "suspected" below "requirement."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the observances by which a child does not carry a staff and does not build a hut are, in principle, sparing in requirement: all editions have a side note reading "doubtful" below ze.

sentences.zh: 按童子不杖、不廬見禮記雜記下，注云：「未成人者，不能備禮也。」

translations.literal: Examining: a child's not staff and not hut appear in Record of Rites Miscellaneous Records, lower; commentary says: "One not yet adult cannot complete ritual."
translations.idiomatic: A child's not carrying a staff and not building a hut appear in Record of Rites, "Miscellaneous Records," lower scroll; the commentary says, "One who is not yet an adult cannot fully observe ritual."

sentences.zh: 這裏是說童子不杖不廬的禮節，於理不該苛責。

translations.literal: Here it is saying that the ritual observances of a child's not staff and not hut—in principle should not be harshly required.
translations.idiomatic: Here the text means that the ritual observances by which a child does not carry a staff and does not build a hut should not, in principle, be harshly required.

sentences.zh: 並無可疑，今刪。

translations.literal: Altogether nothing doubtful—now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing doubtful here; the note is deleted.

sentences.zh: 是有間之言 諸本「間」訛「聞」，不可通，今據冊府卷五八０

translations.literal: Is a statement with qualifications—all editions corrupt "qualification" to "hearing," untenable; now according to Ce fu juan 580
translations.idiomatic: Is a qualified statement: all editions corrupt jian to wen ("hearing"), which will not parse; the text is restored according to Imperial Archives, juan 580
